criteria.deny_return: Deny when the request is over 45 days old, has no original receipt, or a completed inspection confirms use or missing parts.
criteria.none_of_above: Choose when neither substantive outcome applies, including when required evidence is incomplete and the request must remain pending with the returns associate.
criteria.route_to_store_manager: Route for exception review only when the request is 31–45 days old, has an original receipt, and has a completed inspection confirming the merchandise is unused and complete.

decision.instructions: Select the correct current routing outcome under the stated return-exception policy.

input.state: A customer asks to return a boxed espresso machine 38 days after purchase. The standard return window is 30 days. Policy allows a store manager to review days 31–45 only when the returns associate has an original receipt and a completed inspection confirming the item is unused and complete. Requests must be denied if they are over 45 days, lack a receipt, or an inspection confirms use or missing parts. If the inspection is incomplete, the associate must mark the request pending and obtain the missing evidence. The receipt shows purchase on August 4, and the request was made September 11. Box photos were taken, but no inspection was completed.

reference.reason: The receipt establishes a 38-day-old purchase, but box photos do not satisfy the required completed inspection. The request must remain pending with the returns associate, so it cannot yet be routed to the store manager or denied.

criteria.none_of_above: Use only when the evidence is missing, contradictory, or does not satisfy any listed routing rubric.
criteria.returns_associate_denial: The returns associate denies the request if it is beyond 45 days, lacks a verified receipt, is opened or damaged, or is final sale.
criteria.returns_associate_standard_approval: The returns associate approves the return only if it is within the standard 30-day window and otherwise eligible.
criteria.store_manager_exception_review: Route to the store manager when the request is 31–45 days after purchase and the item is receipt-verified, unopened, and not final sale.

decision.instructions: Apply the stated store policy. Select the single route whose complete rubric matches the evidence, paying close attention to negation in the register lookup.

state.context: A customer asks to return a $180 espresso machine 38 days after purchase. The standard return window is 30 days. The returns associate verifies the original receipt and confirms the serial number matches. The box seal is intact, and inspection finds no signs of use or damage. The register lookup states, “This item is not a final-sale SKU.” Store policy allows a store manager to review exceptions from days 31–45 only when the item is unopened, receipt-verified, and not final sale. Associates cannot approve such exceptions.
evidence: Purchase occurred 38 days ago.
Original receipt and matching serial number were verified.
The machine is unopened and undamaged.
The item is not final sale.
state.request: Choose the correct routing decision for this return request.

reference.reason: Route to the store manager because day 38 falls within the 31–45-day exception period, the receipt is verified, the item is unopened, and the lookup explicitly says it is not final sale.

criteria.false: No — do not route it yet because return intent is conditional and at least one stated condition remains unconfirmed.
criteria.true: Yes — route the case now because return intent is unconditional or all customer-stated conditions have been confirmed achievable.

decision.instructions: Decide whether this request is ready to be routed for an in-store return exception review. Under the retailer’s rubric, an otherwise qualifying late return is ready only when the customer has unconditional return intent, or when every condition attached to the customer’s intent has been confirmed achievable. Answer yes or no using the descriptions below.

state.speaker: Customer
state.text: I bought this sealed espresso machine 31 days ago and have the receipt. I’ll return it only if the refund can go back to my original card; if the only option is store credit, I’ll keep it.

state.speaker: Returns associate
state.text: The receipt and purchase date match, and the factory seal is intact. Returns normally close after 30 days, but unopened items through day 37 can be reviewed by a store manager.

state.speaker: Store manager
state.text: Has the original-card refund option been confirmed?

state.speaker: Returns associate
state.text: No. The payment lookup is temporarily unavailable, so I cannot yet confirm whether that refund method is possible.

reference.reason: The item is within the manager-review window and has supporting evidence, but the customer will return it only for an original-card refund. That condition remains unconfirmed because the payment lookup is unavailable, so the readiness rubric is not met.

criteria.false: No — do not route the request; the returns associate should deny it.
criteria.true: Yes — route the request to the store manager for an exception review.

decision.instructions: Using the most recent evidence and the stated policy, decide whether the returns associate should route Elena’s return request to the store manager.

input.state: Customer Elena asks a returns associate to return a $90 countertop mixer 37 days after purchase. The standard return window is 30 days. Store policy says requests 31–45 days after purchase must be routed to the store manager only when the purchase is verified and the item is unopened; otherwise, the associate denies them. At 10:00 a.m., Elena has no receipt, though the factory seals are intact. At 10:20 a.m., she retrieves her digital receipt, and the associate verifies its date, price, and item number against the sales system.

reference.reason: Yes. The temporal update supplies a verified receipt, and the intact factory seals show the mixer is unopened. Because the request is 37 days after purchase, it meets both conditions for manager review of a 31–45-day exception.

criteria: 0 — Associate resolution: The returns associate denies the return under a clear policy rule; no manager review is needed.
1 — Standard manager review: The evidence does not conclusively establish eligibility, so the store manager must verify facts or decide a permitted exception.
2 — High-impact manager intervention: The request is potentially eligible and involves documented severe customer impact requiring immediate manager handling.
decision.instructions: Apply the stated policy and route from low to high intervention. Final-sale merchandise is ineligible even for a manager exception. A matching register transaction record overrides conflicting printed-receipt wording.

state.context: Customer Lena Ortiz asks a returns associate to refund a $74 jacket 38 days after purchase. Standard returns close after 30 days; managers may grant one exception within 45 days only when the item is unworn and not marked final sale. The jacket has tags attached and no visible wear. Store policy says the transaction record controls if a printed receipt conflicts with the register record, provided the transaction ID matches.
evidence: Printed receipt T-88419 says “regular price” and lists a 30-day return window.
Register lookup for matching transaction ID T-88419 shows “FINAL SALE—no return or exception.”
The customer says the final-sale designation must be a register error.
state.request: Select the appropriate routing level for this return request.

reference.reason: The matching register record marks the jacket final sale and controls over the conflicting printed receipt. Final-sale items cannot receive an exception, so the returns associate should deny the request without manager review.

legend.0: 0 — Associate resolution: The returns associate denies the return under a clear policy rule; no manager review is needed.
legend.1: 1 — Standard manager review: The evidence does not conclusively establish eligibility, so the store manager must verify facts or decide a permitted exception.
legend.2: 2 — High-impact manager intervention: The request is potentially eligible and involves documented severe customer impact requiring immediate manager handling.

criteria: 0 — Not reviewable: the matching receipt is missing or invalid, or neither required condition record is available; the associate must obtain core evidence before routing.

1 — Conditionally reviewable: the matching receipt is valid and exactly one of the two required condition records is available; route to the store manager with the missing condition information identified.
2 — Decision-ready: the matching receipt is valid and both the seal inspection and accessories checklist are recorded; the store manager can decide the exception without gathering more evidence.
decision.instructions: Rate the completeness of this 31–45-day return-exception file. Policy requires a valid matching receipt plus two condition records: a seal inspection and a completed accessories checklist. Select the single level that applies.

state.speaker: Customer
state.text: I bought this countertop blender here 38 days ago. It has never been used, and I brought the printed receipt.

state.speaker: Returns associate
state.text: The receipt matches the blender’s SKU and shows a $129 purchase. Our normal return limit is 30 days, so this needs an exception review.

state.speaker: Customer
state.text: The factory seal is still intact. I need to leave soon, so I cannot wait while the box is opened and every accessory is counted.

state.speaker: Returns associate
state.text: I recorded the intact seal, but the required accessories checklist is therefore missing. I can send the request to the store manager with that gap noted.

reference.reason: The request is within the 31–45-day exception window and has a matching receipt and recorded seal inspection, but the required accessories checklist is missing. It is therefore only conditionally reviewable by the store manager.

legend.0: 0 — Not reviewable: the matching receipt is missing or invalid, or neither required condition record is available; the associate must obtain core evidence before routing.
legend.1: 1 — Conditionally reviewable: the matching receipt is valid and exactly one of the two required condition records is available; route to the store manager with the missing condition information identified.
legend.2: 2 — Decision-ready: the matching receipt is valid and both the seal inspection and accessories checklist are recorded; the store manager can decide the exception without gathering more evidence.

criteria.critical_specialist_not_ready: Not ready; Critical defect; route to the category specialist because a safety or regulatory claim contradicts documentation.
criteria.major_seller_correction_not_ready: Not ready; Major defect; route to the marketplace seller for correction because no Critical defect exists and a customer-facing package-contents claim contradicts seller documentation.
criteria.minor_support_not_ready: Not ready; Minor defect; route to marketplace support because no Critical or Major defect exists, but a required non-customer-facing field is missing.
criteria.ready_publish: Ready to publish; no Critical, Major, or Minor defect is present.

decision.instructions: Choose exactly one option. Apply the ordered rubric to the supplied listing fields and seller attachments, treating explicit negation in the packing sheet as decisive evidence about package contents.

state.context: A marketplace seller submitted a cordless desk-lamp listing. The catalog reviewer must assign the highest applicable severity and route. Ordered rubric: Critical—safety/regulatory contradiction, route to category specialist; Major—no Critical issue and a customer-facing package-contents claim contradicts seller documentation, route to seller correction; Minor—neither higher defect applies, but a required non-customer-facing field is missing, route to marketplace support; Ready—no defect. Only Ready listings may be published.
evidence: Listing title: “LumaGo Cordless Lamp with USB-C Charger Included.”
Seller’s signed packing sheet states: “USB-C charger is not included; lamp and charging cable only.”
Compliance attachment confirms the lamp’s battery certification, and every required catalog field is populated.
state.request: Determine publication readiness, highest defect severity, and the correct route under the rubric.

reference.reason: The listing says a USB-C charger is included, while the signed packing sheet explicitly says it is not included. This customer-facing package-contents contradiction is Major. No safety or regulatory contradiction exists, so the listing is not ready and must return to the seller for correction.

criteria.critical_block_no: Not publication-ready; critical severity and blocked because a safety or regulatory claim is directly disproved by documentation.
criteria.major_seller_correction_no: Not publication-ready; major severity and returned to the seller because a required core field is missing or conflicting without qualifying category ambiguity and conditional authorization.
criteria.major_specialist_review_no: Not publication-ready; major severity and routed to a category specialist because both values have documentary support, the category definition is unresolved, and the seller conditionally authorizes the definition-matching value.
criteria.minor_correction_no: Not publication-ready; minor severity and routed for correction because the only defect is cosmetic and does not affect meaning or filtering.
criteria.ready_publish_yes: Publication-ready with no defect because all required fields are complete, consistent, and require no further interpretation.

decision.instructions: Choose the single triage result using this ordered rubric: (1) Critical block—documentation directly disproves a safety or regulatory claim. (2) Major specialist review—not publication-ready when supplied evidence supports two candidate values because a category definition is unresolved, and the seller conditionally authorizes the value matching that definition. (3) Major seller correction—not publication-ready when a required core field is missing or conflicting and the specialist-review condition is not met. (4) Minor correction—not publication-ready for cosmetic defects that do not change meaning or filtering. (5) Ready—every required field is complete, consistent, and needs no review.

state.speaker: Marketplace seller
state.text: I submitted the Northstar Soup Maker with Capacity = 1.7 L. The attached manufacturer sheet states “rated vessel volume: 1.7 L” and “recommended working fill: 1.5 L.”

state.speaker: Catalog reviewer
state.text: All other required fields match the sheet. Capacity is a required core attribute used in search filters, but the category guide supplied here does not say whether capacity means rated vessel volume or working fill.

state.speaker: Marketplace seller
state.text: If this category uses rated volume, keep 1.7 L. If it uses recommended working fill, please set it to 1.5 L; I authorize either value based on the category definition.

state.speaker: Marketplace support agent
state.text: A category specialist can determine which capacity definition applies. The listing remains unpublished while that controlled-field interpretation is pending.

reference.reason: The attachment supports both 1.7 L rated volume and 1.5 L working fill. The unresolved category definition determines which value is valid, and the seller conditionally authorizes either outcome. Under the rubric, this requires major specialist review and the listing is not publication-ready.

criteria.false: No — at least one required listing field conflicts with the latest seller documentation, so correction or specialist review is required.
criteria.true: Yes — all required listing fields match the latest seller documentation, so the listing is publication-ready.

decision.instructions: Decide whether the listing is publication-ready under the supplied policy, using the latest attachment as the controlling evidence.

input.state: On Monday, a marketplace seller submitted an insulated-bottle listing showing 750 mL capacity, stainless-steel material, and dimensions of 24 × 7 cm; the attached specification sheet said 500 mL. On Tuesday, a marketplace support agent confirmed that the seller replaced it with a signed datasheet showing 750 mL and dimensions of 28 × 8 cm. A catalog reviewer checks it Wednesday. Policy says the latest attachment supersedes earlier versions. Publication requires all required fields—capacity, material, and dimensions—to match the latest documentation. Severity ranks: critical for identity or prohibited-item issues, major for a required-field inconsistency, minor for typos, and none for no defect. Major defects route to seller correction; critical defects route to a category specialist.

reference.reason: No. The Tuesday datasheet supersedes Monday’s sheet and resolves the capacity conflict, but its 28 × 8 cm dimensions conflict with the listing’s 24 × 7 cm dimensions. This is a major required-field inconsistency and must be routed to seller correction.

criteria.false: No — do not require specialist review; treat the listing as ready or eligible for ordinary correction.
criteria.true: Yes — route the listing to a category specialist and block publication pending resolution.

decision.instructions: Answer yes or no by applying the stated triage policy to the supplied evidence.

state.context: A marketplace support agent asks a catalog reviewer to triage a fictional Voltara travel kettle listing. Policy ranks defects Blocker > Major > Minor. Any unresolved conflict between seller documents about voltage is a Blocker and must be routed to a category specialist; a seller’s unsupported statement does not resolve it. Blockers prevent publication.
evidence: The listing and attached user manual specify 220–240 V.
The attached compliance certificate identifies the same model number, VT-K7, but specifies 120 V.
The marketplace seller says the certificate is outdated, but supplies no replacement certificate or revision history.
All other required listing fields are complete and consistent.
state.request: Should the reviewer route the listing to a category specialist as a publication-blocking defect?

reference.reason: Yes. The manual and compliance certificate conflict on voltage for the same model, and the seller provides no documentation resolving the conflict. Policy therefore classifies it as a Blocker requiring category-specialist review before publication.

criteria: 0 — Complete: No required or optional listing information is missing, and all supplied documentation is consistent with the listing. Publication ready: yes.

1 — Minor incomplete: One or more optional merchandising fields are missing, but all required identity, offer, category, and product-specification fields are present and consistent. Route for routine correction without blocking publication. Publication ready: yes.

2 — Major incomplete: At least one required non-safety field is missing or unsupported, such as package quantity, material, dimensions, price, or product identity. Route to the seller for correction before publication. Publication ready: no.

3 — Specialist-required incomplete: Missing information concerns safety, regulatory compliance, restricted-product status, or unresolved category identity and cannot be resolved from seller documentation. Route to a category specialist. Publication ready: no.
decision.instructions: Choose the single highest applicable completeness-severity level. Treat unsupported information as missing rather than inferring it. Apply the publication-readiness judgment included in each level.

state.speaker: Marketplace seller
state.text: I submitted the fictional Northpine 350 ml stoneware mug. The listing includes title, category, price, package quantity of one, dimensions, material, color, capacity, and three photos. The care-instructions field is blank.

state.speaker: Catalog reviewer
state.text: The attached supplier sheet confirms every entered specification and shows the same model code, NP-M350. It contains no washing or microwave-care information, so I cannot safely infer care instructions.

state.speaker: Marketplace seller
state.text: There are no additional documents. In the Drinkware category, care instructions are an optional merchandising field; all required identity, offer, and product-specification fields are complete.

state.speaker: Marketplace support agent
state.text: Please determine the listing’s completeness severity and whether it may be published under the stated rubric.

reference.reason: The only missing information is care guidance, and both the supplier sheet and seller confirm it is unavailable. Because care instructions are explicitly optional while every required field is complete and consistent, this is a minor completeness defect that does not block publication.

legend.0: 0 — Complete: No required or optional listing information is missing, and all supplied documentation is consistent with the listing. Publication ready: yes.
legend.1: 1 — Minor incomplete: One or more optional merchandising fields are missing, but all required identity, offer, category, and product-specification fields are present and consistent. Route for routine correction without blocking publication. Publication ready: yes.
legend.2: 2 — Major incomplete: At least one required non-safety field is missing or unsupported, such as package quantity, material, dimensions, price, or product identity. Route to the seller for correction before publication. Publication ready: no.
legend.3: 3 — Specialist-required incomplete: Missing information concerns safety, regulatory compliance, restricted-product status, or unresolved category identity and cannot be resolved from seller documentation. Route to a category specialist. Publication ready: no.

criteria: 0 — No defect: All in-scope required fields and attachments are complete and consistent; only explicitly permitted exceptions may be present. Publish as submitted.

1 — Minor defect: An in-scope cosmetic or optional-field issue exists that does not affect product identity, included items, technical use, or compliance. Publication may proceed with a nonblocking correction request.

2 — Major correctable defect: A required in-scope field is missing or conflicts with clear seller documentation, but the correct value is directly supported and no specialist judgment is needed. Block publication and return to the seller for correction.

3 — Specialist-review defect: Safety, regulatory, category eligibility, or materially conflicting documentation makes the correct listing content uncertain. Block publication and route to a category specialist.
decision.instructions: Select the highest applicable defect-severity level. Apply the stated scope and exception. A listing is publication-ready only at levels 0 or 1; level 2 requires seller correction, and level 3 requires category-specialist review.

input.state: A marketplace seller submits a rechargeable desk-lamp listing. The title says “Ocean Blue Clamp Lamp,” while the seller’s specification PDF calls the color “Navy”; both show swatch ID B17. Marketplace support confirms that color-name differences are exempt when swatch IDs match. The listing’s required “input voltage” field is blank, although the PDF clearly states “5 V DC.” Its package-contents field lists the lamp, clamp, and USB-C cable, matching the attachment. Policy scope covers required technical fields and package contents, but excludes qualifying color-name differences. A catalog reviewer must determine publication readiness and routing.

reference.reason: The B17 color-name difference is explicitly exempt, but the required input-voltage field is blank even though the seller PDF provides an unambiguous value. This is an in-scope required-field omission that blocks publication and can be corrected directly without specialist interpretation.

legend.0: 0 — No defect: All in-scope required fields and attachments are complete and consistent; only explicitly permitted exceptions may be present. Publish as submitted.
legend.1: 1 — Minor defect: An in-scope cosmetic or optional-field issue exists that does not affect product identity, included items, technical use, or compliance. Publication may proceed with a nonblocking correction request.
legend.2: 2 — Major correctable defect: A required in-scope field is missing or conflicts with clear seller documentation, but the correct value is directly supported and no specialist judgment is needed. Block publication and return to the seller for correction.
legend.3: 3 — Specialist-review defect: Safety, regulatory, category eligibility, or materially conflicting documentation makes the correct listing content uncertain. Block publication and route to a category specialist.

criteria.apply_credit_keep_annual: Add the $24 credit and preserve the annual subscription when the offer and pre-renewal acceptance are verified and the correction request is within seven calendar days.
criteria.execute_fallback_cancellation: Cancel annual, move to monthly, and process the permitted unused-term refund only when the credit is ineligible and the subscriber expressly supplied this fallback.
criteria.none_of_above: Use only when the evidence satisfies none of the four resolution rubrics above.
criteria.route_duplicate_payment_review: Route for duplicate-payment investigation only when the account shows at least two settled subscription charges for the disputed renewal.
criteria.seek_intent_clarification: Ask the subscriber to clarify only when neither the primary conditional request nor any fallback identifies an actionable outcome.

decision.instructions: Choose the authorized resolution. Policy: an omitted retention credit may be added when a valid offer was recorded and accepted before renewal and correction is requested no later than seven calendar days after renewal. Conditional acceptance counts when its condition is applying that eligible credit. If the credit is ineligible, follow an expressly stated fallback request; otherwise seek clarification. Duplicate-payment routing requires two settled charges.

state.speaker: Subscriber
state.text: Invoice INV-8841 shows a $240 annual renewal on September 14 with no $24 retention credit. On September 13 I replied, “Yes, I’ll keep annual provided the promised credit is applied.” If you can still apply it, leave everything annual; if not, cancel annual, move me to monthly, and refund the unused annual term.

state.speaker: Billing support agent
state.text: The retention offer was logged September 13 at 4:10 p.m., and the subscriber’s quoted acceptance arrived at 7:02 p.m. Renewal posted September 14 at 2:00 a.m. The offer code is valid for annual renewals, but it was omitted from INV-8841.

state.speaker: Subscription operations analyst
state.text: Today is September 20. No adjustment, cancellation, monthly-plan invoice, or second renewal payment appears on the account. The original $240 payment is settled.

reference.reason: Apply the $24 credit and retain the annual plan. The valid offer and conditional acceptance both preceded the September 14 renewal, and September 20 is within the seven-day correction window. Because the credit is eligible, the subscriber’s fallback cancellation condition does not activate.

criteria.duplicate_subscription_payment: Use only when two or more settled payments cover the same subscription period; pending, released, or voided authorizations do not qualify.
criteria.none_of_above: Use when the latest verified unresolved issue falls outside all five listed routes, including an invoice tax correction.
criteria.plan_change_mismatch: Use only when the current unresolved issue is a requested plan upgrade or downgrade that was not applied correctly.
criteria.promotional_credit_missing: Use only when a verified valid promotion remains unapplied to the current invoice.
criteria.refund_posting_delay: Use only when the merchant has issued a refund and it remains unposted after the stated processing period.
criteria.renewal_charge_dispute: Use only when the current unresolved issue is the base renewal charge being unauthorized or billed at the wrong standard price, excluding tax, promotions, plan changes, and later-voided invoices.

decision.instructions: Route the case by its latest verified unresolved billing issue. Earlier issues superseded by later timeline updates must not determine the route. Select exactly one option whose rubric fits the evidence.

input.state: Subscriber Mira Chen disputed a $48 annual renewal on September 2, saying a promotion should have reduced it. Billing support agent Leo verified on September 3 that the promotion expired August 31. On September 5, the original invoice was voided and its card authorization released; replacement invoice R-204 for $44 then settled once. On September 6, subscription operations analyst Priya approved Mira’s tax-exemption certificate effective August 30 and confirmed that R-204 incorrectly includes $4 sales tax. No tax credit or corrected invoice has been issued. Mira’s latest request is only for correction of that $4 tax charge.

reference.reason: The latest unresolved issue is an incorrectly charged $4 sales tax after retroactive tax-exemption approval. The promotion was expired, the original renewal invoice was voided, and only one replacement payment settled. No substantive option covers tax correction, so none_of_above applies.

criteria.false: The case is not verified as eligible because the evidence, resolved under policy, shows fewer than two settled captures.
criteria.true: The case is verified as eligible for a duplicate-payment adjustment because two renewal captures settled.

decision.instructions: Answer yes only if the evidence verifies that two captures for the same renewal both settled. Answer no if fewer than two captures settled, applying the stated conflict-resolution rule.

state.context: Subscriber Mara Venn disputes her July 3 Pro plan renewal. A billing support agent opened a duplicate-payment case, and a subscription operations analyst reviewed the payment records. Policy grants an adjustment only when two captures for the same renewal have both settled. When records conflict, the final settlement ledger overrides invoice payment labels and pending bank entries.
evidence: Invoice INV-7308 lists payment references P441 and P442, each labeled “Paid — $84.”
The subscriber’s bank screenshot shows two $84 entries, but one is marked “pending.”
The final settlement ledger shows P441 settled for $84 and P442 was an authorization-only transaction voided on July 5 with $0 captured.
state.request: Verify whether this case qualifies for a duplicate-payment adjustment under the stated policy.

reference.reason: No. Although the invoice labels both references as paid, the controlling final settlement ledger shows only P441 settled; P442 captured $0 and was voided.

criteria.false: No — all required evidence is present, so operations can decide duplicate-payment adjustment eligibility now.
criteria.true: Yes — required evidence is missing, so route the case for missing-information collection before deciding adjustment eligibility.

decision.instructions: Completeness task: Should this case be classified as incomplete and routed for missing-information collection before duplicate-payment adjustment eligibility is decided? Under policy, review is ready only when evidence identifies the account, amount, currency, date, and confirms that both disputed charges are posted rather than pending or processing. If any required element is missing, answer yes; otherwise answer no.

state.speaker: Subscriber
state.text: My StreamForge Plus renewal was $84.00 on September 12. My bank app shows two entries with descriptor STREAMFORGE*PLUS: one marked posted and another marked processing. I uploaded the receipt for the posted charge only.

state.speaker: Billing support agent
state.text: Account SF-48219 has one annual Plus renewal invoice, INV-7714, for $84.00 USD dated September 12. The billing ledger currently contains only one settled payment.

state.speaker: Subscription operations analyst
state.text: The matching amount and descriptor suggest a possible duplicate, but the second entry has no bank statement, processor receipt, or posted transaction identifier. Its final settlement status cannot yet be verified.

state.speaker: Subscriber
state.text: I cannot download a statement for the second entry unless it changes from processing to posted.

reference.reason: Yes. The second $84.00 entry is still marked processing, and no statement, processor receipt, or posted transaction identifier confirms settlement. Matching descriptors and amounts alone do not satisfy the explicit readiness policy.

criteria: No adjustment: the case is ineligible and the authorized amount is exactly $0.
Minimal adjustment: an account credit or refund from $0.01 through $24.99 is authorized.
Moderate adjustment: a partial refund from $25.00 through $59.99 is authorized.
High adjustment: a refund from $60.00 through $120.00 on one invoice is authorized.
Very high adjustment: more than $120.00 is authorized, or corrections must cover multiple paid invoices.
decision.instructions: Determine the authorized adjustment impact level using the policy exception, not the subscriber’s requested amount. Calculate the prorated difference and select exactly one level.

input.state: Subscriber Maya Chen disputes invoice R-841, a $120 Premium annual renewal charged on September 14. On September 16, after two elapsed service days, she asked billing support agent Leo Grant to downgrade her to the $72 Basic annual plan and refund the full renewal. Account logs show no Premium features were used. Subscription operations analyst Priya Nair reviews the policy: renewal charges are normally outside refund scope, except downgrades requested within 72 hours with no premium use. That exception authorizes only the prorated annual price difference for the remaining 363 of 365 days, rounded to cents.

reference.reason: The downgrade falls within the 72-hour, no-premium-use exception, but that exception allows only the prorated price difference: ($120 − $72) × 363/365 = $47.74. This is a partial refund between $25.00 and $59.99.

legend.0: No adjustment: the case is ineligible and the authorized amount is exactly $0.
legend.1: Minimal adjustment: an account credit or refund from $0.01 through $24.99 is authorized.
legend.2: Moderate adjustment: a partial refund from $25.00 through $59.99 is authorized.
legend.3: High adjustment: a refund from $60.00 through $120.00 on one invoice is authorized.
legend.4: Very high adjustment: more than $120.00 is authorized, or corrections must cover multiple paid invoices.

criteria: 0 — Renewal-charge review: Use when the disputed charge is a scheduled renewal and no later evidence identifies a different charge as the unresolved issue.

1 — Plan-change proration review: Use when the subscriber disputes the legitimate amount or timing of a single upgrade or downgrade charge, without a repeated settled payment for the same service period.
2 — Promotional-credit review: Use when the unresolved issue is an advertised, promised, or documented discount or credit that was omitted or misapplied.

3 — Duplicate-payment review: Use when the referenced unresolved charge is a second settled payment duplicating another payment for the same subscription service period, even if it followed a plan change.
4 — No billing-adjustment route: Use when all referenced charges were accepted, reversed already, merely pending, or unsupported by invoice or payment evidence.
decision.instructions: Select the single best routing level. Resolve pronouns from the surrounding dialogue and account timeline. Apply the first level whose definition matches the referenced unresolved charge.

state.context: Mara, a subscriber, contacted billing support after renewing and upgrading her fictional StreamForge subscription. A subscription operations analyst must route the unresolved dispute using the invoices and dialogue.
evidence: September 1: Basic renewed for $120 on invoice R-410; the card payment settled.
September 3: Mara upgraded to Pro for a prorated $36 on invoice U-882; the payment settled and covers September 3–30.
September 4: invoice U-889 charged another settled $36 for Pro coverage from September 3–30.
Mara said, “The renewal is fine, and I expected the first upgrade charge. The second $36 is the problem; please reverse it.”
The billing support agent noted, “She wants it refunded because it repeats the payment for the same Pro service period.”
state.request: Which billing queue should the subscription operations analyst select for the charge referenced by “it” in the agent’s note?

reference.reason: “It” refers to the second $36 charge Mara identified as the problem, not the accepted renewal or first upgrade charge. Invoices U-882 and U-889 are settled payments of the same amount for the same Pro service period, so the duplicate-payment queue applies.

legend.0: 0 — Renewal-charge review: Use when the disputed charge is a scheduled renewal and no later evidence identifies a different charge as the unresolved issue.
legend.1: 1 — Plan-change proration review: Use when the subscriber disputes the legitimate amount or timing of a single upgrade or downgrade charge, without a repeated settled payment for the same service period.
legend.2: 2 — Promotional-credit review: Use when the unresolved issue is an advertised, promised, or documented discount or credit that was omitted or misapplied.
legend.3: 3 — Duplicate-payment review: Use when the referenced unresolved charge is a second settled payment duplicating another payment for the same subscription service period, even if it followed a plan change.
legend.4: 4 — No billing-adjustment route: Use when all referenced charges were accepted, reversed already, merely pending, or unsupported by invoice or payment evidence.

criteria.approve_exact_item: Approve only when the picker located the originally requested item, so no substitution is being made.
criteria.approve_proposed_substitute: Approve only when the latest customer note permits the proposed replacement and all stated item attributes match.
criteria.none_of_above: Choose when policy requires an action not represented by any substantive option.
criteria.reject_without_replacement: Reject the item only when the latest note forbids every substitution, or when every customer-named alternative has been confirmed unavailable.
criteria.route_customer_contact: Send to the customer contact agent only when the latest note is ambiguous or conflicting and names no usable alternative.
criteria.route_supervisor_review: Send to the fulfillment supervisor only when there is a documented safety, regulatory, or price-limit exception requiring authorization.

decision.instructions: Choose the single correct route or decision under the stated policy. Apply the latest customer update and select none_of_above if the required action is not represented by a substantive option.

input.state: At 8:40, a pickup customer noted, “Any plant-based milk is fine.” The ordered unsweetened oat beverage was unavailable, so the store picker proposed a sweetened almond beverage. At 9:11, before the 9:15 fulfillment decision, the customer updated the note: “No almond or other nut drinks. Unsweetened soy is okay.” Soy availability has not been checked. Store policy says the latest timestamped note supersedes earlier notes. When a proposal is barred but the latest note names an acceptable alternative with unknown availability, the order must return to picking to check that alternative; it must not yet be approved, rejected, escalated, or sent for customer contact.

reference.reason: The 9:11 update supersedes the 8:40 note and bars the proposed almond beverage while naming unsweetened soy. Because soy availability is unknown, policy requires returning the order to picking, but no substantive option represents that route.

criteria.contact_customer_for_exception: Pause fulfillment and ask the pickup customer whether to accept this otherwise plausible replacement because it violates a clear controlling preference while contact is still possible.
criteria.send_to_picking: Approve the proposed replacement for picking because it satisfies every controlling item restriction.
criteria.send_to_supervisor_review: Escalate because the governing records cannot be reconciled using the stated precedence policy or necessary facts are unavailable.

decision.instructions: An item-specific note overrides a general checkout note. A substitution toggle permits only replacements satisfying applicable notes. Route to picking when the proposal meets all controlling restrictions. Route to customer contact when a plausible replacement violates a clear preference and the contact window remains open. Route to supervisor review only when controlling records are ambiguous, irreconcilable under the policy, or required facts are missing.

state.context: Pickup customer Maya ordered two 32-ounce cartons of plain, unsweetened oat milk. The requested item is unavailable. The store picker proposes two same-size cartons of vanilla, sweetened oat milk from the same brand. Pickup is scheduled in 70 minutes.
evidence: Maya’s checkout note says, “If oat milk is out, any same-brand oat milk is okay.”
The item-specific note says, “Plain and unsweetened only—no flavored or sweetened substitutes.”
The item’s substitution toggle is enabled, and the customer-contact window closes 30 minutes before pickup.
state.request: Choose the correct route for the proposed substitution under the stated routing policy.

reference.reason: The item-specific note controls and excludes both flavored and sweetened replacements. Because the proposed oat milk violates that clear restriction but the contact window remains open for another 40 minutes, customer contact is required rather than picking or supervisor review.

criteria.false: No — at least one explicit substitution constraint is contradicted or remains unverified without a customer waiver, so fulfillment may not approve the replacement yet.
criteria.true: Yes — every explicit substitution constraint is verified or the customer has clearly waived any unverified constraint, so fulfillment may approve the replacement.

decision.instructions: Readiness task: Decide whether fulfillment may approve the proposed substitution now. Under store policy, approval requires every explicit customer constraint to be positively verified. An unverified required attribute cannot be assumed from product similarity. If any required attribute is unknown and the customer has not waived it, the correct decision is no and the order must be routed to customer contact or supervisor review.

state.text: My order note says: “Substitutions are fine only if they are the same brand, exactly 16 ounces, and labeled no added sugar.”

state.speaker: Store picker
state.text: The requested North Mill creamy peanut butter is unavailable. I found North Mill smooth peanut butter in a 16-ounce jar. The shelf tag and front label confirm the brand and size, but the nutrition-side photo is obscured, so I cannot verify whether it is labeled no added sugar.

state.speaker: Fulfillment supervisor
state.text: The pickup window closes in 12 minutes. Determine whether this replacement is ready for fulfillment approval.

reference.reason: No. Brand and 16-ounce size are verified, but the required “no added sugar” label is unknown because the relevant photo is obscured. The customer has not responded or waived that condition, so the replacement is not ready for approval.

criteria.false: No — do not approve the replacement for picking; route it to customer contact or supervisor review as policy requires.
criteria.true: Yes — approve the replacement and route the order to picking.

decision.instructions: Decide whether the proposed substitution is approved and ready to be routed to picking. Answer yes or no using the descriptions provided.

input.state: Pickup customer Lena ordered one 20-ounce can of BrightStart Stage 2 infant formula for $24. The item is unavailable. The store picker proposes one 22-ounce can of BrightStart Stage 2 for $25.50. Lena’s order note says, “Substitutions are allowed across this order if the replacement costs no more than 10% extra; for infant formula, use the same brand and stage only.” Fulfillment policy says an explicit category exception narrows the general permission. A replacement meeting both the general price limit and the exception may be sent to picking. Failed matches go to customer contact, while only ambiguous cases require supervisor review.

reference.reason: Yes. The $25.50 replacement is only 6.25% above $24, within the 10% order-wide limit, and it satisfies the infant-formula exception because both brand and stage are unchanged. The case is unambiguous and can proceed to picking.

criteria: 0 — Unsuitable: Reject the proposed substitution because it clearly conflicts with an explicit customer restriction; do not pick the replacement.
1 — Uncertain: Do not approve yet; route to the customer contact agent because the note or item match is genuinely ambiguous and customer clarification is required.
2 — Suitable: Approve the substitution because it satisfies the stated item attributes and all applicable customer notes.
decision.instructions: Choose exactly one level. Apply the customer’s note by resolving its references in context; matching item attributes does not override an explicit no-substitution instruction.

state.context: Pickup customer Lena ordered a 16-ounce Sunrise sesame loaf and strawberry jam. Her order note says, “The sesame loaf is for Maya; if it is unavailable, do not substitute that one. Any brand is fine for the jam.” The Sunrise loaf is unavailable. The store picker proposes a 16-ounce Harvest sesame loaf. The proposed loaf matches the requested size and sesame variety, but it is a different brand.
The customer explicitly prohibited replacing the referenced loaf when unavailable.
state.request: Rate the proposed loaf substitution using the three-level suitability rubric.

reference.reason: The note’s “it” and “that one” corefer with the sesame loaf, so the customer explicitly forbade this replacement despite its matching size and variety. Fulfillment must reject it without needing clarification.

criteria.ledger_correction_restore_200: Route to Ledger Correction to replace the erroneous 240-point removal with a 40-point adjustment, restoring 200 points.
criteria.manual_record_reconciliation: Route for additional transaction research because the available records do not establish how much merchandise was returned or retained.
criteria.valid_full_return_removal: Close the claim as invalid because reliable records establish a full return and justify removal of all 240 points.

decision.instructions: Route based on the supplied records. Use Ledger Correction when purchase identity and retained eligible value are established but the points adjustment is wrong. Use Valid Full-Return Removal when records establish that all merchandise was returned. Use Manual Record Reconciliation only when conflicting records leave the returned or retained value unresolved.

state.context: Loyalty member Mara Chen reports that 240 points from her 8 August purchase disappeared after she returned one item. A customer service representative confirmed the purchase number and escalated the claim to a rewards program analyst. Program policy awards one point per eligible dollar and removes points only for returned value.
evidence: Receipt RC-8841 shows $240 of eligible merchandise and Mara’s loyalty ID.
The loyalty ledger initially added 240 points, then removed all 240 with the notation “full return.”
The store’s item-level return record links RC-8841 to a single $40 item; the other $200 was retained.
No other return or payment reversal appears for RC-8841.
state.request: Choose the correct loyalty workflow for the claim.

reference.reason: The ledger’s full-return notation conflicts with the more specific item-level return record. The receipt and return record establish $200 in retained eligible merchandise, so only 40 points should have been removed and 200 points must be restored.

criteria.incomplete_request_required_records: Select when the issue is a purchase-points claim but at least one required system field—the delivered-at date or eligible-merchandise subtotal—is missing.
criteria.ready_invalid_earning_claim: Select only if both required system fields are present and prove that no points are currently missing or due.
criteria.ready_valid_earning_discrepancy: Select only if both required system fields are present and prove that fewer points posted than were due after the waiting period.
criteria.wrong_loyalty_workflow: Select only if the reported issue concerns reward redemption or tier status rather than points earned from a purchase.

decision.instructions: Classify the claim’s workflow readiness. Apply the option rubrics exactly; the asserted delivery date being at the seven-day boundary does not count as a system record.

state.text: Order K-184 totaled $218. I expected about 200 points, but none appeared. My receipt combines merchandise and tax, and I remember the package arriving September 10.

state.speaker: Customer service representative
state.text: The loyalty account shows no pending or posted points for K-184. The order export says “Delivered” and lists only the $218 total; it omits both the eligible-merchandise subtotal and delivered-at date.

state.speaker: Rewards program analyst

state.speaker: Loyalty member
state.text: Today is September 17. Can the claim be decided now?

reference.reason: This is an earning claim, but both required verification fields—the system-recorded delivery date and eligible-merchandise subtotal—are missing. The $218 combined total and the member’s recollection cannot establish whether points are due.

criteria.false: No — the gift-card exclusion applies, so Priya was not entitled to the claimed points.
criteria.true: Yes — the records and applicable rules show that Priya should have received the claimed 200 points.

decision.instructions: Decide whether Priya's claim for 200 missing points is valid under the supplied program and promotion rules. Answer yes or no.

input.state: Loyalty member Priya Shah reports 200 missing Cedar Circle points after buying a $100 gift card during a double-points weekend. The customer service representative routed the claim to the missing-points workflow. Account records show zero points awarded, and the receipt confirms the entire purchase was one gift card. Program rules award one base point per dollar on eligible merchandise but exclude gift-card purchases. The promotion advertised double points on “all purchases,” yet its scope clause limits doubling to transactions that first qualify for base points and does not override listed exclusions. A rewards program analyst must verify the claim against these records.

reference.reason: The claim is invalid because the purchase consisted entirely of a gift card, which is excluded from base-point eligibility. The promotion only doubles transactions already eligible for base points and does not override that exception.

criteria.false: The disputed points are not tied to a canceled reward redemption and should be routed elsewhere.
criteria.true: The disputed points are tied to a canceled reward redemption and should be routed to Reward Redemption Reversal.

decision.instructions: Resolve the coreference in the representative’s note, then apply the supplied routing policy. Answer yes or no.

state.context: A loyalty member disputes a points balance after two June purchases. A customer service representative recorded her explanation, and a rewards program analyst must select the correct workflow.
evidence: Account ledger: June 4 blender reward redemption deducted 1,200 points; June 6 mug redemption deducted 400 points.
Representative note: “She canceled the blender order that afternoon. The card charge was refunded, but those points never came back.”
Policy: Route points not restored after cancellation of a reward order to Reward Redemption Reversal. Route absent points from a completed earning transaction to Missing Earned Points.
state.request: Should the analyst route this claim to Reward Redemption Reversal?

reference.reason: Yes. “Those points” refers contextually to the 1,200 points deducted for the canceled blender redemption, not the later 400-point mug redemption. Because they were not restored after cancellation, the policy routes the claim to Reward Redemption Reversal.

criteria: Level 0: No verified discrepancy; net missing points equal exactly 0.
Level 1: Minor verified discrepancy; net missing points are 1 through 99.
Level 2: Moderate verified discrepancy; net missing points are 100 through 499.
Level 3: Major verified discrepancy; net missing points are 500 or more.
decision.instructions: Verify the net missing-point discrepancy. Compute expected balance as opening balance plus eligible posted earnings minus authorized posted redemptions. Exclude gift-card spending, tier status, and pending promotions. Net missing points equal max(expected balance minus actual balance, 0). Select the matching magnitude level.

state.speaker: Loyalty member
state.text: My balance should be higher after order K-184. I spent $500 and expected 500 points. I also reached Gold last week and have a 300-point birthday offer pending.

state.speaker: Customer service representative
state.text: The account opened the claim period with 2,000 points. It now shows 1,750 points after a posted 700-point reward redemption.

state.speaker: Rewards program analyst
state.text: Order K-184 contained $450 of eligible merchandise and a $50 gift card. Policy awards one point per eligible merchandise dollar; gift cards earn none. The ledger posted 450 points for the order.

state.speaker: Customer service representative
state.text: Gold status does not change the earning rate, and pending promotional points are excluded until posted. The member confirms the 700-point redemption was authorized.

reference.reason: Expected balance is 2,000 + 450 - 700 = 1,750, exactly matching the actual balance. The $50 gift card, Gold status, and pending 300-point offer are distractors excluded by policy, so verified missing points are 0.

2 — Moderate discrepancy: the recorded deduction is 1,001 to 5,000 points above the required amount, inclusive.

decision.instructions: Verify the redemption discrepancy, then select the level matching the number of points deducted above the policy-required amount. Treat paraphrased terms in the claim according to the clarification in the state.

input.state: A loyalty member tells a customer service representative, “I used a fifteen-dollar coupon on my June 8 order, but four thousand credits vanished from my account.” The representative routes the claim to a rewards program analyst. The redemption record confirms a $15 reward was applied and 4,000 points were deducted. The supplied program policy states that redemption costs 200 points per $1 of reward value. No other account adjustments occurred that day. In the member’s wording, “credits vanished” refers to points deducted during redemption.

reference.reason: A $15 reward should cost 3,000 points at 200 points per dollar, but the record shows 4,000 deducted. The 1,000-point excess is an exact boundary included in level 1.

criteria.level_1_unready: Level 1 — An unresolved item has no appropriate owner; stop the handoff and assign ownership.
criteria.level_2_major_gaps: Level 2 — All unresolved items have owners, but two or more required evidence fields are missing; return for substantial revision.
criteria.level_3_one_gap: Level 3 — All unresolved items have appropriate owners, but exactly one required evidence field is missing; keep the routing and return for the missing evidence.
criteria.level_4_complete: Level 4 — Every unresolved item has an appropriate owner, current status, timestamp, and record link; accept the handoff as complete.

decision.instructions: Evaluate completeness and routing. Every unresolved item requires an appropriate owner, current status, update timestamp, and record link. Use the ordered readiness scale: Level 1 if any unresolved item lacks an owner; Level 2 if owners are assigned but at least two required evidence fields are missing; Level 3 if owners are assigned and exactly one required evidence field is missing; Level 4 if no required evidence is missing. Select the matching readiness level and action.

state.speaker: Outgoing shift lead
state.text: The 18:00 handoff lists Line 2 pump vibration as unresolved: “monitoring, no production impact,” updated at 17:42 and assigned to the operations coordinator. The maintenance-record link is blank.

state.speaker: Incoming shift lead

state.speaker: Outgoing shift lead
state.text: There is no pump maintenance-record link yet; all other listed fields are current.

reference.reason: The unresolved pump item is correctly assigned to the operations coordinator and has a status and timestamp, but its required record link is missing. Exactly one evidence field is absent, so the handoff is Level 3 and should be returned for that link while ownership remains unchanged.

criteria.level_1_not_ready: Confirmed scope; at least one in-scope item lacks required evidence or owner acceptance and is not covered by a valid evidence exception.
criteria.level_2_exception_ready: Confirmed scope; the only evidence gap is covered by a valid coordinator-approved temporary evidence exception that names an owner and deadline.
criteria.level_3_ready_with_follow_up: Confirmed scope; every unresolved in-scope item has all required evidence, including acceptance by the appropriate owner, but at least one accepted follow-up remains open.
criteria.level_4_complete: Confirmed scope; every in-scope item has all required evidence, and no unresolved item awaits owner acceptance.
criteria.none_of_above: No substantive level can be assigned because the applicable scope has not been established under policy.

decision.instructions: Select the applicable handoff-readiness result. Use the ordered substantive scale from Level 4 (highest) to Level 1 (lowest). Required evidence for each in-scope unresolved item is current status, a timestamped artifact, the appropriate named owner, and owner acceptance. Apply an exception only when its scope is established under the stated policy.

input.state: At 19:00, outgoing shift lead Mara submits the handoff to incoming shift lead Dev. The master scope includes scrubber S-2, while an operations-coordinator-approved exception register excludes S-2 through 23:00; both records were updated at 18:45. Policy says conflicting scope records must be reconciled by operations coordinator Inez before readiness is rated, and neither record takes precedence. If S-2 is in scope, its status and telemetry are present, but its unresolved alarm was routed to the controls engineer without owner acceptance. If excluded, every remaining in-scope item is complete. Inez is unavailable and has not reconciled the conflict.

reference.reason: None of Levels 1–4 applies because each requires confirmed scope. The equally current master scope and approved exception conflict, and policy requires coordinator reconciliation before rating. S-2 would make the handoff Level 1 if included, while excluding it would make the handoff Level 4.

criteria.false: No — at least one Ready requirement is missing; assign the applicable lower readiness level under the rubric.
criteria.true: Yes — all Ready requirements are satisfied, including explicit acknowledgment by each unresolved item's owner.

decision.instructions: Resolve references using speaker attribution, then apply the stated rubric. Answer yes only if the handoff qualifies as Ready.

state.context: At the 06:00 shift change, unresolved equipment alerts must be routed to the operations coordinator. A handoff is Ready only if a status-board export from the prior 30 minutes is attached, every unresolved item has the correct owner and that owner explicitly acknowledges it, and the incoming lead accepts the shift. It is Conditional only when all evidence is present but incoming acceptance is pending; otherwise it is Not ready.
evidence: Outgoing shift lead Nia: “The 05:44 board export is attached. Chiller alert C-7 remains. Marco has C-7. Eli, did you acknowledge that alert?”
Incoming shift lead Eli: “Yes, I did. I accept the shift.”
Operations coordinator Marco provides no acknowledgment in the record.
state.request: Is this handoff Ready? Also determine whether C-7 was correctly routed and whether the required owner acknowledgment is present.

reference.reason: C-7 was correctly routed to operations coordinator Marco, but “I” in “Yes, I did” refers to incoming lead Eli, not Marco. Because the actual owner never acknowledged C-7, required evidence is missing, so the handoff is Not ready.

criteria.false: No — the handoff is either Conditional or Not Ready because at least one in-scope production item fails a required evidence, routing, action, or acknowledgment condition.
criteria.true: Yes — the handoff is Ready, the highest level, because every in-scope production item satisfies the evidence and routing requirements.

decision.instructions: Decide whether the handoff earns the highest readiness rating. Evaluate only production items; facilities announcements are distractors. Required evidence for every production item is a current status and a timestamped artifact. Each unresolved item also needs a named appropriate owner, a next action, and that owner’s acknowledgment. Ordered scale: Ready = all requirements met; Conditional = status and artifact are present, but an unresolved item lacks valid routing or acknowledgment; Not Ready = any production item lacks status or a timestamped artifact. Question: Is the handoff rated Ready?

state.speaker: Outgoing shift lead
state.text: Line 4 pump vibration is the only unresolved production item. Status at 17:42: stable at 6.1 mm/s. Trend snapshot TS-144 is attached. Ticket M-882 assigns the 20:00 inspection to maintenance duty engineer Mara Chen.

The completed filter swap has a timestamped work order and photo. The freezer and parking notices are explicitly out-of-scope distractors.

criteria: 0 — Not ready: At least one unresolved operational item lacks a required status artifact, is routed to the wrong or no owner, or lacks an accurate own-word paraphrase from the incoming lead.
1 — Minimally ready: Every unresolved item has the required artifact, correct owner, and valid paraphrase, but at least one owner has not acknowledged receipt.
2 — Provisionally ready: All required fields and owner acknowledgments are present, but at least one unresolved item lacks a follow-up time or completion checkpoint.
3 — Ready: Required evidence, routing, paraphrases, acknowledgments, and follow-up checkpoints are complete; only minor nonoperational clarification remains.
4 — Fully ready: Every item is fully documented, correctly routed, paraphrased, acknowledged, and scheduled, with no clarification or correction needed.
decision.instructions: Rate the handoff’s readiness using the ordered rubric. Check the routing, required status evidence, and whether the incoming lead supplied a valid paraphrase.

input.state: At 18:00, outgoing shift lead Mara records an unresolved freezer temperature alarm: “Zone 3 remains at 11°C; inspect the compressor before restarting.” Policy requires each unresolved item to include a timestamped status artifact, routing to the responsible owner, and an incoming shift lead’s own-word paraphrase of the status and next action; copied wording does not count. Facilities handles refrigeration alarms. Mara attaches no sensor screenshot and routes the item to the inventory planner. Incoming shift lead Dev repeats Mara’s sentence verbatim. Operations coordinator Lena must score the handoff before shift change.

reference.reason: The unresolved refrigeration alarm is routed to the inventory planner instead of Facilities, lacks the required timestamped status artifact, and Dev copied Mara’s wording rather than paraphrasing it. These mandatory failures make the handoff not ready.

legend.0: 0 — Not ready: At least one unresolved operational item lacks a required status artifact, is routed to the wrong or no owner, or lacks an accurate own-word paraphrase from the incoming lead.
legend.1: 1 — Minimally ready: Every unresolved item has the required artifact, correct owner, and valid paraphrase, but at least one owner has not acknowledged receipt.
legend.2: 2 — Provisionally ready: All required fields and owner acknowledgments are present, but at least one unresolved item lacks a follow-up time or completion checkpoint.
legend.3: 3 — Ready: Required evidence, routing, paraphrases, acknowledgments, and follow-up checkpoints are complete; only minor nonoperational clarification remains.

criteria: 0 — Not ready: The record provides no usable current status evidence, or unresolved critical work has neither a next action nor an identifiable owner; the incoming shift cannot safely act from it.

1 — Low readiness: Some items have usable evidence, but at least one critical unresolved item lacks required status evidence, has no next action, or is routed to the wrong owner. Substantial correction is required before acceptance.

2 — Conditionally ready: Every critical item has required evidence, a next action, and the correct owner, but a routine item is missing evidence or correct routing, or the incoming acknowledgement is still pending.

3 — Ready: Every unresolved item has required current evidence, a next action, and the correct owner, and the incoming shift lead has acknowledged the handoff. Only inconsequential presentation issues may remain.
4 — Fully verified: Level 3 is met, and each unresolved item also includes timestamped verification of owner acceptance, an escalation or contingency path, and a clearly stated completion criterion.
decision.instructions: Select the single readiness level that best fits the explicit record. Treat required status artifacts, routing, and acknowledgements as mandatory under the stated policy; do not infer missing evidence.

state.context: At 18:00, the packaging operations team changes shifts. Policy requires every unresolved item to include a current status artifact, next action, and correct owner. 2 — Conditional readiness: Requirements are documented, and any remaining required setup or equipment gaps have been routed to the correct teams with confirmed completion before class; proceed only after the setup checklist confirms completion.
3 — High readiness: Every documented requirement is already present, functional, and arranged as specified, with the setup checklist complete and no required tasks open.
decision.instructions: Rate operational readiness using the ordered rubric. Consider only documented lesson requirements; unrelated room defects and unused backup equipment are distractors. Route technology or adapter work to the instructional technology technician, furniture arrangement to the facilities coordinator, and learning-material preparation to the teaching assistant. Select the single best level index.

input.state: For a 10:00 fictional biology lesson, the classroom instructor’s plan documents 24 movable chairs in six groups of four, one working display, an HDMI adapter, and 24 microscope worksheets. Room B12 has 24 chairs, but the setup checklist shows them still in rows. The facilities coordinator confirms the chairs can be grouped by 9:20. The installed display passed today’s test; a spare projector in storage has a failed lamp. The HDMI adapter is absent from B12, but the instructional technology technician confirms a tested adapter can be delivered by 9:15. The teaching assistant has counted 24 worksheets. A broken wall clock and a scratched podium are also reported, but neither is required by the plan.

reference.reason: All requirements are documented, and the display and worksheets are ready. Two required setup gaps remain, but both have correct owners and confirmed completion before 10:00: Facilities will group the chairs by 9:20, and Instructional Technology will deliver the tested HDMI adapter by 9:15. The failed spare projector, broken clock, and scratched podium are irrelevant distractors. The session is therefore conditionally ready pending checklist confirmation.

criteria.confirm_direct_replacement: Confirm a replacement requiring no transfer, with ticket validity, seat availability, and arrival evidence established.
criteria.confirm_feasible_connection: Confirm a transfer itinerary because ticket validity and capacity are established and timetable evidence proves the transfer meets or exceeds the stated minimum.
criteria.none_of_above: Choose when no substantive classification is supported, including when required timetable evidence is missing and neither feasibility nor infeasibility can be proved.
criteria.reject_infeasible_connection: Reject the itinerary because timetable evidence proves the transfer interval is shorter than the stated minimum.
criteria.route_operations_support: Route the traveler to operations support because the evidence identifies unavailable capacity, a canceled replacement, or an unresolved platform or service-control issue.
criteria.route_ticket_support: Route the traveler to ticket support because the evidence identifies invalid, restricted, or uncertain ticket acceptance.

decision.instructions: Classify the proposed Orwick itinerary’s rebooking readiness using only the supplied evidence. Select exactly one option. input.state: At Brindle Central, rail traveler Mara holds a flexible ticket to Lanton valid on any same-day Brindle–Lanton service. Her 13:40 direct train is canceled. reference.reason: The proposed connection cannot be confirmed or rejected because the 14:05 train’s arrival time at Orwick is missing. Although the 12-minute minimum is known, no transfer interval can be calculated, and no ticket, capacity, or operational issue requires a support queue.

state.context: Mara, a rail traveler, asks station rebooking agent Ivo after the 14:10 Northport–Lake City train is canceled. She has a valid flexible ticket and states she cannot use stairs. Train operations coordinator Sela supplies the live plan.

A: 14:35, stair-only transfer, arrives 16:10.
B: 14:42; same-platform connection 15:20–15:27, confirmed held by Sela; arrives 16:30.

input.state: Rail traveler Mara holds a valid flexible ticket from Alderwick to Bellhaven. Her 15:10 direct train is canceled. 2 — Most suitable: the route is valid, feasible, meets every hard constraint, and offers the best eligible balance—earliest arrival first, then fewer transfers unless the traveler confirms another priority.

state.context: At fictional Harbor Lantern Hotel, guest Mara Venn asks the front desk agent to assign a room meeting her reservation’s hard requirements: two separate beds and a roll-in shower. A quiet location is preferred, not required.

Rank verified hard requirements first, then preferences; place pending rooms above conflicting rooms.

input.state: At the fictional Juniper Quay Hotel, guest Mara Venn reserved two beds and a documented roll-in shower as hard requirements; a quiet courtyard room is a preference. Room 214 is clean and released, has two beds, a registry-documented roll-in shower, and faces the courtyard. Room 408 is clean and released, has two beds, a harbor view, and a minibar, but the accessibility registry lists only a standard tub. Mara recalls an online photo showing a roll-in shower in 408. Room 310 has the required features but housekeeping has not released it. Policy: hard requirements outrank preferences; undocumented accessibility claims go to the property accessibility coordinator, while release questions go to the housekeeping supervisor. The front desk agent proposes assigning 408 and ranking it above 214.

reference.reason: No. Room 408’s roll-in shower is not documented; the registry instead lists a standard tub. Its harbor view and minibar are distractors because they do not satisfy a hard requirement. Room 214 is released and meets both hard requirements, so it ranks above 408. The disputed photo claim should be routed to the property accessibility coordinator.

Accessibility counts as documented only in the accessibility register or written coordinator confirmation. Exclude rooms failing any requirement; rank survivors by quietness, then readiness. Route undocumented accessibility claims to the property accessibility coordinator and readiness disputes to housekeeping.
evidence: The hotel guest says, “I cannot cross a shower curb.”

state.request: Should the front desk assign 514 as the top-ranked compliant room?

Room 214 ranks second with three mandatory requirements and quiet, but explicitly lacks a visual alarm. Room 118 ranks third with three mandatory requirements but has a queen bed and is noisy. decision.instructions: Assess assignment readiness for the highest-ranked available room. Mark each mandatory requirement yes or no, counting only documented features; an explicit negation overrides a marketing claim. Rank rooms first by number of mandatory requirements fulfilled, breaking ties in favor of a documented roll-in shower, then bedside clearance, and finally the quiet-floor preference. Select one level. If no room fulfills every mandatory requirement, route the case according to the stated policy.

input.state: At fictional Larkspur Hotel, hotel guest Mira Chen’s reservation lists three mandatory requirements: a documented roll-in shower, at least 32 inches of bedside clearance, and feather-free bedding; a quiet floor is only a preference. The front desk agent has two clean, available rooms. Room 214’s inventory documents a roll-in shower, 30-inch clearance, feather-free bedding, and a quiet-floor location. Room 310 has 34-inch clearance and feather-free bedding. Although its marketing note claims a roll-in shower, the accessibility register explicitly says Room 310 does not have one. The housekeeping supervisor confirms both bedding records. No other rooms are available tonight. Accessibility shortfalls go to the property accessibility coordinator; bedding uncertainties go to housekeeping.

reference.reason: Room 214 ranks above Room 310. Each fulfills two of three mandatory requirements, but Room 214 wins the tie because its roll-in shower is documented. Room 310’s shower is a no because the accessibility register explicitly says it does not have one, overriding the marketing claim. Room 214 fulfills the shower and bedding requirements but fails the 32-inch clearance requirement with only 30 inches. The case therefore goes to the property accessibility coordinator.
