criteria.basic_inspection_hold_high: Route to basic inspection, prohibit reuse, and assign high urgency; applies when evidence shows moisture originating from the appliance but no active flooding or electrical signs.
criteria.cleanup_hold_moderate: Route to cleanup, do not use the washer again yet, and assign moderate urgency; applies when a spill is external but its source remains uncertain.
criteria.deferred_maintenance_reuse_moderate: Route to deferred maintenance, permit reuse, and assign moderate urgency; applies when logs show a recurring non-safety fault that does not prevent normal cycles.
criteria.load_correction_reuse_low: Route to load correction, permit reuse, and assign low urgency; applies when cycle notes confirm an unbalanced or overloaded load without leakage.
criteria.none_of_above: Select when none of the other options exactly matches the evidence-based route, reuse decision, and urgency.

decision.instructions: Select the one option whose route, reuse decision, and urgency all exactly match the explicit evidence and policy. Urgency is ordered low < moderate < high < emergency. If no substantive option matches all three fields, select none_of_above.

input.state: Resident Mara reports, “The washer leaked during spin; I found blue liquid beside it.” Household maintenance coordinator Joel reviews the 9:10 p.m. photo, which shows blue liquid trailing from an uncapped detergent bottle on the shelf to the floor, with no moisture under the washer. The cycle log shows a normal completion and no error code. Inspector Nia records dry inlet hoses, drain hose, door seal, and machine base, then identifies a matching drip on the bottle. Policy: confirmed external product spills route to cleanup, permit appliance reuse, and receive low urgency. Appliance-origin moisture instead requires basic inspection and no reuse.

reference.reason: The photo, normal cycle log, dry appliance components, and matching bottle drip confirm an external detergent spill. Policy therefore requires cleanup, reuse permitted, and low urgency. No substantive option contains that exact combination.

criteria.basic_inspection_hold_U2: Choose only for a first unexplained appliance symptom without electrical, heat, or flooding danger; pause use pending prompt inspection, urgency 2.
criteria.basic_inspection_stop_U3: Choose when a repeatable leak or other appliance fault is supported; stop using the washer until inspected, urgency 3.
criteria.cleanup_resume_U1: Choose when evidence identifies a non-appliance source and records no washer symptom; clean the area, resume washer use, urgency 1.
criteria.deferred_maintenance_resume_U2: Choose only when a minor appliance defect is confirmed but safe operation is unaffected; resume use and schedule maintenance, urgency 2.
criteria.hazard_shutdown_U4: Choose only for active flooding, smoke, sparking, shock risk, or another immediate hazard; shut off utilities, prohibit use, urgency 4.
criteria.load_correction_resume_U1: Choose only when imbalance, overloading, or incorrect loading caused the event; correct the load, resume use, urgency 1.

decision.instructions: Choose exactly one option. Apply the stated policy to the photos, cycle log, symptom notes, and inspection findings. The negated facts must be treated as evidence, not as missing information.

state.context: A resident claims the washer leaked onto the laundry-nook floor. Policy: route to cleanup when evidence identifies a non-appliance source and no washer symptom; load correction for imbalance or overfilling; basic inspection for an unexplained or repeatable appliance symptom; deferred maintenance for a minor confirmed defect that does not affect safe operation. Urgency runs 1 (routine), 2 (prompt), 3 (stop use), 4 (immediate hazard).
evidence: The resident’s photo shows a puddle extending from beneath the utility sink toward the washer.
The cycle log shows the washer was not running during the reported time.
The resident’s symptom note reports no unusual sound, odor, code, or failed cycle.
The household maintenance coordinator found the sink basin wet and its drain temporarily blocked.
The appliance inspector found no moisture on the washer cabinet, hoses, or hose connections.
state.request: Verify the leak claim, select the route, decide whether washer use may resume, and assign urgency.

reference.reason: The claimed washer leak is contradicted: the washer was not running, and inspection found no moisture on it or its connections. The wet, blocked sink and puddle path identify a non-appliance source, so only routine cleanup is needed and washer use may resume.

criteria.false: No — at least one stated condition for the resident’s intended reuse remains unfulfilled, even if the incident otherwise appears routine.
criteria.true: Yes — the evidence establishes readiness for the resident’s intended reuse, including fulfillment of every stated condition.

decision.instructions: Answer whether the washer is ready for the resident’s intended reuse. Routing options are cleanup, load correction, basic inspection, and deferred maintenance. Urgency is ordered: 1 = routine, 2 = prompt, 3 = urgent, 4 = immediate shutdown. Under the household policy, an isolated banging event with an off-center single item, no leak, odor, scraping, looseness, or damage routes to load correction at urgency 1. However, when the resident expressly conditions reuse on a specified test, readiness is established only after that test is completed successfully. An inspection plan or other favorable evidence does not satisfy the condition.

state.speaker: Resident reporting the incident
state.text: The washer banged twice during spin with one wet bath mat inside. I stopped it. I will use it again only if an inspector completes a balanced empty spin without banging.

state.speaker: Household maintenance coordinator
state.text: The cycle log shows cancellation at minute 31, during high spin. The resident’s photo shows the washer level, no water outside, and the bath mat folded against one drum wall.

state.speaker: Person inspecting the appliance
state.text: I opened the drum and found no looseness, odor, scraping, or visible damage. This fits an unbalanced single-item load, but I have not run the requested empty-spin test because the laundry nook outlet is currently inaccessible behind storage boxes.

reference.reason: The evidence supports load correction at urgency 1, but the resident conditioned reuse on a successful balanced empty-spin test. That test was not performed, so the washer is not yet ready for the intended reuse.

criteria.false: The evidence supports another route, continued stop-use status, or urgency above U1.
criteria.true: The latest verified evidence supports cleanup rather than appliance repair, and the washer is safe to use again with urgency U1.

decision.instructions: Decide whether the report should be routed to cleanup, with the washer approved for reuse at urgency U1. Use the latest verified temporal update when it corrects an earlier claim. Route to cleanup when evidence identifies an external spill and inspection plus a test run show no appliance leak. Route to load correction for imbalance or overloading, basic inspection for an unresolved appliance symptom, and deferred maintenance for a non-urgent confirmed defect. Urgency is ordered: U1 routine, U2 prompt, U3 urgent, U4 stop-use emergency.

input.state: At 8:10 a.m., resident Maya reported a palm-sized blue puddle beside the washer after starting a normal cycle and claimed the washer was leaking. At 8:18, the household maintenance coordinator paused the appliance. Maya’s 8:22 photo showed an uncapped blue-detergent bottle tipped on the shelf directly above the puddle. The cycle log showed a completed wash with no error or unexpected fill. At 8:35, inspector Leon dried the area, found the supply hoses, drain hose, door seal, and washer underside dry, and ran a five-minute rinse with no new liquid. Maya then confirmed she had knocked over the bottle before starting the wash.

reference.reason: Yes. The later photo and Maya’s confirmation identify spilled blue detergent, while the cycle log, dry inspection points, and leak-free rinse contradict the initial washer-leak claim. Under the rubric, this is cleanup; the washer may be reused at routine U1 urgency.

criteria: 0 — Low urgency: Route to cleanup or load correction when evidence identifies an external spill or loading issue and appliance checks show no recurring fault. Clean or correct the load, then normal use is allowed.

1 — Moderate urgency: Route to basic inspection when the source remains ambiguous, a symptom repeats, or logs and physical checks conflict without confirming a hazardous defect. Pause use until hoses, seals, venting, leveling, or load balance are checked.

2 — High urgency: Route to deferred maintenance and remove the appliance from use when inspection or repeat operation confirms an appliance leak, electrical or burning symptom, uncontrolled heat, damaged component, or repeated error. Arrange repair before reuse.
decision.instructions: Choose exactly one ordered disposition level. Apply the higher level only when its stated conditions are met; an unsupported resident claim alone does not override direct inspection and a successful repeat check.

state.context: Mara, the resident, reports that the washer “leaked during spin” and asks whether it is safe to run again. Devon, the household maintenance coordinator, must assign a route and urgency. Inez inspected the laundry nook after the cycle.
evidence: Mara’s photo shows a small puddle beside the washer, supporting her leak claim.
Inez’s wider photo shows an uncapped detergent bottle lying above the puddle; the washer hoses, door seal, underside, and floor directly beneath the machine are dry.
The cycle log records a normal completion with no error codes. Inez ran a short rinse afterward and observed no dripping or recurrence.
state.request: Select the disposition level using corroborated photos, logs, and inspection findings; explain how the conflicting evidence affects reuse.

reference.reason: Level 0 is warranted. Although Mara’s close photo makes the puddle look like a washer leak, the wider photo identifies a spilled detergent bottle, inspection found all washer leak points dry, and the logged cycle plus repeat rinse showed no fault. Clean the spill; the washer may be used again.

legend.2: 2 — High urgency: Route to deferred maintenance and remove the appliance from use when inspection or repeat operation confirms an appliance leak, electrical or burning symptom, uncontrolled heat, damaged component, or repeated error. Arrange repair before reuse.

criteria: 0 — Low response: Cleanup or load correction; reuse is allowed now only when all required evidence is present, shows no ongoing leak or danger indicator, and supports a one-time spill or load-balance cause.

1 — Moderate response: Basic inspection before reuse; apply when the incident is minor and contained with no level-2 indicator, but required evidence is missing or a simple load-related cause remains unconfirmed. Complete the inspection the same day before another cycle.

2 — High response: Stop use and arrange urgent maintenance; apply for active or recurring leakage, water near an outlet, smoke, sparks, electrical odor, repeated fault logs, or failure of the basic inspection.
decision.instructions: Assign one response-intensity level using the ordered rubric. Required evidence for immediate reuse is: incident-area photos including rear connections, the cycle log, and symptom notes covering recurrence after unloading. Missing required evidence prevents level 0. Determine the route, whether the washer may be used again, and the urgency.

state.speaker: Resident reporting the incident
state.text: The washer left a small puddle after I washed one heavy blanket. The photo shows clear water under the front-left corner. I saw no smoke, sparks, or water near the outlet.

state.speaker: Household maintenance coordinator
state.text: The cycle log shows an unbalanced-load warning, but the cycle completed. Did anyone photograph the rear hoses and drain connection or note whether dripping continued after unloading?

state.speaker: Person inspecting the appliance
state.text: I wiped up about three tablespoons of water. The floor stayed dry for 20 minutes with the washer off, but I could not reach the rear connections, so there is no rear photo or hose-condition note.

reference.reason: The small contained puddle, unbalanced-load log, and absence of smoke, sparks, continued dripping, or water near the outlet do not meet level 2. However, rear-connection photos and hose-condition notes are missing, so immediate reuse under level 0 is not permitted. Route to a same-day basic inspection before another cycle.

legend.0: 0 — Low response: Cleanup or load correction; reuse is allowed now only when all required evidence is present, shows no ongoing leak or danger indicator, and supports a one-time spill or load-balance cause.
legend.1: 1 — Moderate response: Basic inspection before reuse; apply when the incident is minor and contained with no level-2 indicator, but required evidence is missing or a simple load-related cause remains unconfirmed. Complete the inspection the same day before another cycle.
legend.2: 2 — High response: Stop use and arrange urgent maintenance; apply for active or recurring leakage, water near an outlet, smoke, sparks, electrical odor, repeated fault logs, or failure of the basic inspection.

criteria.level_0_indeterminate: Readiness cannot be rated because evidence about at least one required recipe or safety condition is absent.
criteria.level_1_discard: Not recoverable: contamination or another stated violation requires discarding the affected food.
criteria.level_2_major_correction: A required cooking or timed heating step is unmet; route the food back to the home cook and stove before serving.
criteria.level_3_minor_correction: A recoverable non-heating recipe error remains, such as adding a present ingredient or correcting portions.
criteria.level_4_portion_only: Cooking is complete, but only portioning, garnishing, labeling, or another non-heating finish remains.
criteria.level_5_ready: Fully ready: every recipe and kitchen-rule requirement is complete; serve now or seal labeled storage portions.

decision.instructions: Choose exactly one ordered readiness level. Apply the first description that matches the evidence; unmet required heating is a major correction even when all other steps are complete.

state.context: The meal planner’s recipe for four teriyaki tofu bowls requires cooked rice, browned tofu, and glaze that bubbles continuously for two minutes before serving. Kitchen rules say any unmet timed cooking step requires return to the stove; garnish or portion adjustments do not. The home cook handles heat, the ingredient prep helper handles garnish, and the cleanup helper labels refrigerated portions.
evidence: Rice is fully cooked, and the tofu is browned on every listed side.
The glaze was warmed and stirred, but it did not bubble at any point.
Bowls are portioned; two storage containers are labeled and ready.
No ingredients are missing, and nothing is contaminated.
state.request: Rate current readiness and select the required next workflow step.

reference.reason: The glaze did not bubble, so the recipe’s required two-minute bubbling step was not completed. Under the kitchen rules, the home cook must return it to the stove; therefore the meal needs a major correction before serving.

criteria.LEVEL_1_FAILED_DISCARD: A cooking or cooling limit was missed, or the stated condition requires discard; do not serve or store the affected food.
criteria.LEVEL_2_READY_CORRECTION_DUE: Cooking and portioning comply, and no safety limit was breached, but a triggered corrective or storage action is still pending; transfer the rice now into shallow labeled containers and refrigerate.
criteria.LEVEL_3_COMPLETE: All recipe, portioning, and triggered storage steps have already been completed; serve the dinner portions and leave the leftovers refrigerated.

decision.instructions: Choose the single overall workflow level. The levels are ordered from Level 3 (complete) to Level 1 (failed). Apply the cook’s conditional storage intent at the inclusive temperature boundary.

state.speaker: Meal planner
state.text: The bowl recipe requires chicken at 74°C or higher, rice divided into two 350 g dinner portions, and leftover rice cooled from 60°C to 21°C or lower within two hours. Thresholds are inclusive.

state.speaker: Home cook
state.text: Cooling began at 6:00 p.m. If the leftover rice is 21°C or lower at 8:00, I intend it to go immediately into shallow labeled containers in the refrigerator; if it is above 21°C, discard it.

state.speaker: Ingredient prep helper
state.text: At 8:00 exactly, the chicken reads 74°C, both dinner portions weigh 350 g, and the leftover rice reads exactly 21°C.

state.speaker: Cleanup helper
state.text: The leftover rice is still in the cooling bowl on the counter; no shallow containers have been filled yet. Which readiness level and route apply?

reference.reason: Chicken and portions meet their inclusive recipe thresholds, and rice reached exactly 21°C within two hours. That condition triggers refrigeration, not discard, but the required transfer remains undone, so the workflow is Level 2.

criteria.false: No — the meal is at Level 1 or Level 2 because setup is incomplete or a corrective cooking step is still required.
criteria.true: Yes — the meal is at Level 3 or Level 4 because all required cooking checks have passed and no corrective step remains.

decision.instructions: Use the latest temporal update and classify readiness on this ordered rubric: Level 1 = setup incomplete; Level 2 = cooking or another corrective step required; Level 3 = ready to serve; Level 4 = safely portioned and stored. Answer yes only if the meal is currently at Level 3 or Level 4. Is the meal currently ready to serve?

input.state: At 6:10 p.m., the meal planner issued the recipe: roast all chicken pieces until every piece reaches 74°C, then portion with rice and broccoli; refrigerate extra portions within two hours. The ingredient prep helper used separate boards for raw chicken and vegetables. At 6:40, the home cook measured two pieces at 76°C and began plating. At 6:43, a newly checked thick piece measured only 70°C. Under the kitchen rule, one low piece means the entire chicken batch returns to the cooking station until every piece passes 74°C. The cleanup helper has clean storage containers ready, but no portions have been stored yet.

reference.reason: No. The latest check at 6:43 found a chicken piece at 70°C, below the required 74°C. The rule routes the entire batch back to cooking, so the meal is at Level 2 despite the earlier passing measurements.

criteria.false: No — assign Level 1 or Level 2 because a safety, cooking, portioning, or timely-storage requirement remains unmet.
criteria.true: Yes — assign Level 3: serve the two designated portions now and continue cooling the two storage portions.

decision.instructions: Answer the yes/no readiness question using this ordered rubric: Level 1 = unsafe or unusable, so stop and discard; Level 2 = not yet ready, so route to a corrective cooking, portioning, or storage step; Level 3 = recipe cooking checks passed, serving portions are prepared, and storage portions have begun compliant cooling within two hours. Apply the stated kitchen rule when visual and thermometer evidence conflict.

state.context: Home cook Mara is making paprika chicken and rice. Ingredient prep helper Sol measured the recipe’s listed amounts; meal planner Inez checks compliance; cleanup helper Dev handles cooling and storage.
evidence: Recipe: simmer sauce, then cook chicken until a calibrated probe gives two readings of at least 74°C; divide into four equal portions.
Mara recorded 75°C and 74°C in the thickest pieces, although Sol reported that one cut piece still looked slightly pink.
Inez confirmed the probe passed its ice-water calibration today. The kitchen rule says valid probe readings override meat color.
Dev placed two equal portions for serving and two in labeled shallow containers; the storage timer shows 18 minutes since cooking ended.
state.request: Is this meal at Level 3 readiness, allowing serving now and routing the remaining portions to cooling?

reference.reason: The two calibrated readings meet the recipe’s 74°C threshold, and the rule makes them controlling despite the conflicting pink appearance. Four equal portions were made, with two ready to serve and two already routed to labeled shallow containers only 18 minutes after cooking.

criteria: 0 — Serve and portion immediately, treating baking time and appearance as sufficient despite the explicit temperature rule.
1 — Hold the chicken but discard it or restart the entire meal without first obtaining the missing temperature reading.
2 — Notice that the temperature is undocumented, yet begin serving or portioning while planning to check only a later piece.
3 — Do not serve or portion the chicken; measure the thickest piece now, cook further if it is below 74°C, and proceed to portioning and timely refrigeration only after a compliant reading.
decision.instructions: Rate the best readiness and routing decision under the supplied recipe and kitchen rule. The ordered levels measure decision quality, including whether missing required evidence is handled correctly.

state.speaker: Meal planner
state.text: Tonight’s recipe is lemon chicken, rice, and broccoli. Bake chicken 22 minutes at 220°C, then verify at least 74°C in the thickest piece. Kitchen rule: elapsed time, color, and clear juices cannot replace that reading.

state.speaker: Ingredient prep helper
state.text: Chicken was trimmed and seasoned at the raw-meat station. Rice and broccoli were prepared separately with clean tools.

state.speaker: Home cook
state.text: The chicken baked exactly 22 minutes and looks opaque with clear juices. Rice and broccoli are finished, but I did not record or announce a thermometer reading. Can I portion four dinners now?

state.speaker: Cleanup helper
state.text: Four clean containers are ready. Any unserved portions must be refrigerated within two hours, but the meal has not yet been portioned.

reference.reason: The chicken meets the stated time and visual cues, but the required 74°C thermometer reading is missing. The defensible action is to hold portioning and service, route the chicken back to temperature verification, and cook further only if the measured temperature is below 74°C.

criteria: Not ready—at least one in-scope mandatory food-safety requirement fails, or contamination still requires correction; the meal must not be served.
Safe but incomplete—all in-scope safety requirements pass, but at least one required component still needs cooking, resting, draining, or portioning.
Ready with a minor in-scope presentation or workflow issue—all required components are safe and complete, but a non-safety serving step remains; explicit exceptions do not count.
Fully ready—all required components are safe, cooked, rested or drained as specified, and portioned for immediate serving, with no unresolved in-scope issue.
decision.instructions: Rate the meal’s current readiness to serve using the ordered levels below. Apply requirements only to the stated readiness scope; do not lower the rating for explicit exceptions. A mandatory food-safety failure takes precedence over otherwise completed components.

input.state: For Tuesday dinner, the meal planner specifies lemon chicken, rice, and broccoli. The recipe requires chicken to reach 74°C, rice to rest covered for five minutes, and broccoli to be drained before serving. The home cook measures the thickest chicken piece at 68°C. The ingredient prep helper routes it back to the oven; the rice has rested six minutes and the broccoli is drained. The cleanup helper washes the raw-chicken board and notes that an unused mixing bowl remains dirty. Readiness covers only the three required meal components. Optional parsley, unused equipment, and storage of leftovers after dinner are explicit exceptions.

reference.reason: The chicken is only 68°C, below the recipe’s mandatory 74°C requirement, and has been routed back to the oven. Rice and broccoli are complete, while the dirty unused bowl and later leftover storage are out-of-scope exceptions. Therefore the meal is not safe to serve.

legend.0: Not ready—at least one in-scope mandatory food-safety requirement fails, or contamination still requires correction; the meal must not be served.
legend.1: Safe but incomplete—all in-scope safety requirements pass, but at least one required component still needs cooking, resting, draining, or portioning.
legend.2: Ready with a minor in-scope presentation or workflow issue—all required components are safe and complete, but a non-safety serving step remains; explicit exceptions do not count.
legend.3: Fully ready—all required components are safe, cooked, rested or drained as specified, and portioned for immediate serving, with no unresolved in-scope issue.

criteria.final_placement_pass: Pass inspection and move to final divider placement because orientation, fasteners, diagonal tolerance, and load stability all satisfy the rubric.
criteria.step_correction: Disassemble or repeat an assembly step because orientation is wrong for the conditionally determined use, or because diagonal difference is greater than 3 mm.
criteria.tightening: Keep the current assembly sequence but tighten connectors because at least one is proud, loose, or allows joint movement.

decision.instructions: Select the inspection route under this rubric. Choose step correction if panel orientation conflicts with the conditionally determined final use or if diagonal difference exceeds 3 mm. Choose tightening if orientation is correct but any connector is proud, loose, or permits joint movement. Choose final placement/pass only if orientation matches final use, connectors are flush and stable, diagonal difference is 3 mm or less, and the load test shows no sway.

state.speaker: Household assembler
state.text: I fitted the white face of the back panel toward the room. I intend to use the shelf as a freestanding divider if it passes the load test; otherwise I will place it against the wall.

state.speaker: Parts checker
state.text: All listed parts are present and undamaged. The instructions require the white face toward the room for divider use, but toward the wall for wall placement. A diagonal difference of up to and including 3 mm is acceptable.

state.speaker: Household assembler
state.text: The two diagonal measurements are 1200 mm and 1203 mm. Every cam and bolt is snug and flush, and hand pressure does not move any joint.

state.speaker: Final-use tester
state.text: With the specified 20 kg distributed load, the shelf remained level and showed no sway. Therefore, under the assembler’s stated condition, it will be used as a freestanding divider.

reference.reason: The successful load test activates the assembler’s conditional intent to use the shelf as a divider, and the white face is correctly oriented for that use. Connectors are flush and stable, the 3 mm diagonal difference is exactly within the inclusive limit, and the loaded shelf does not sway.

criteria.none_of_above: Choose when none of the three issue routes fits the latest evidence, including when the build now passes inspection and is ready for final placement.
criteria.parts_sorting: Route to parts sorting only when the latest evidence shows a missing, damaged, extra, or substituted component; do not use for assembly or fastening issues.
criteria.step_correction: Route to step correction only when all required parts are present but the latest evidence shows an incorrect orientation, sequence, hole choice, or other mismatch with the instructions; do not use for a fastening-only defect.
criteria.tightening: Route to tightening only when the latest test still shows looseness or wobble while the parts and assembly configuration are otherwise correct.

decision.instructions: Using only the latest applicable evidence, choose the correct current routing. Earlier defects that were successfully corrected do not count as current issues.

input.state: In the living-room workshop, a household assembler built the fictional Alderline three-shelf unit. At 14:00, the build photo showed the middle shelf level and all dowels in the instruction diagram’s marked holes, but the final-use tester found a slight side-to-side wobble. The parts checker confirmed that no parts were missing, damaged, or substituted. At 14:20, the assembler tightened the four rear cross-brace screws as specified in step 8. In a new photo, the brace orientation still matches the instructions. At 14:25, the tester repeated the load and push tests; the unit stayed square, stable, and wobble-free.

reference.reason: The latest temporal update shows that tightening fixed the wobble, all parts and assembly steps match the instructions, and the shelf passes final testing. It should proceed to final placement, but that route is not among the substantive options.

criteria.false: No — at least one mandatory condition fails, so the cabinet must be corrected and reinspected.
criteria.true: Yes — all mandatory inspection conditions are verified, so the cabinet passes final inspection.

decision.instructions: Answer the yes/no inspection question using the stated pass rule and conflict-resolution policy. If any required condition fails, the item does not pass and should be routed to step correction before reinspection.

state.context: In a living-room workshop, a household assembler has finished a fictional Alderline C-4 cabinet. The supplied inspection rule says it passes only if the back panel’s smooth face points inward, both anti-tip straps are installed, and the cabinet does not rock during final-use testing. When notes conflict with timestamped images, the later image controls.
evidence: The assembler’s 14:10 build note says, “Reversed the back panel so the smooth face is now inside; both straps fitted.”
A 14:24 close-up from the parts checker shows the rough face inside and the panel’s labeled exterior edge visible through the cabinet opening.
At 14:30, the final-use tester reports no rocking and photographs both anti-tip straps secured.
state.request: Does the cabinet pass final build inspection?

reference.reason: The later 14:24 image overrides the conflicting 14:10 note and shows the back panel facing the wrong way. Because every listed condition is mandatory, the cabinet fails and requires step correction despite being stable and strapped.

criteria.false: No — approve the unit for final placement without reopening it, treating the assembler’s note and successful use test as sufficient evidence.
criteria.true: Yes — withhold the unit from final placement and route it to step correction so the concealed back-panel orientation can be exposed, verified, and documented; rate the issue minor.

decision.instructions: Verification decision: Should the Larkspur unit be withheld from final placement and routed to step correction for reopening and documented orientation verification? Rubric: a build passes only when every safety test passes and each concealed-orientation checkpoint has either a required progress image or current visual confirmation. Notes alone do not satisfy that checkpoint. If only the required evidence is missing, severity is minor but the item must still be withheld and reopened for verification.

state.speaker: Household assembler
state.text: The Larkspur three-shelf unit is square, all eight cam locks are tightened, and my notes say the back panel’s grooved face was installed inward at step 6.

state.speaker: Parts checker
state.text: The hardware count matches the instructions. However, the required step-6 photo is missing; the only image was taken after the rear trim concealed the panel edges.

state.speaker: Final-use tester
state.text: With 12 kg distributed across the shelves, it does not wobble or creak. The wall strap is fitted, but I cannot visually confirm the concealed back-panel orientation.

state.speaker: Household assembler
state.text: I deleted the step-6 photo accidentally. Confirming the orientation now would require removing the rear trim.

reference.reason: Yes. Load stability, hardware, and wall-strap checks pass, but the required image or current visual confirmation of the concealed back-panel orientation is absent. Under the explicit rubric, notes alone are insufficient, making step correction and verification necessary despite otherwise good build quality.

criteria: 0 — Unsafe or unusable: structural damage, severe instability, or an assembly error creates an immediate collapse or injury risk; stop use and disassemble or replace affected parts.

1 — Major correction required: missing or wrongly oriented structural parts, skipped steps, or multiple inaccessible fastening errors require parts sorting or substantial step correction before retesting.

2 — Minor correction required before placement: the build is otherwise complete and correctly assembled, but one or a few accessible fasteners need tightening, or unloaded wobble exceeds 4 mm; route to tightening and retest.

3 — Standard pass: all in-scope parts and steps are correct, accessible fasteners are secure, unloaded wobble is 4 mm or less, and only excluded matters such as rear-only cosmetic marks or pending wall anchoring remain.
4 — Excellent pass: meets level 3 and also has clean visible surfaces, consistently flush joints, even shelf alignment, and no observed wobble during the unloaded test.
decision.instructions: Rate assembly readiness using the five ordered levels. Consider parts, step accuracy, fastening, and unloaded stability. Ignore wall anchoring and rear-only cosmetic marks under the stated scope. Apply the explicit exception that unloaded wobble above 4 mm prevents a passing level even when wall anchoring is not yet required. Select one level and identify the appropriate route implied by that level.

input.state: In a living-room workshop, a household assembler finishes the fictional Alderline five-shelf unit. The parts checker confirms every listed panel, cam, dowel, and screw is present and correctly oriented; build notes and two photos match instruction steps 1–12. A final-use tester finds no cracking or leaning, but the unloaded top corner moves 5 mm because one accessible cam is loose. The manual permits at most 4 mm. A shallow scratch is visible only on the rear panel. Wall anchoring and rear-only cosmetic marks are outside this inspection’s scope, except unloaded wobble above 4 mm must still be corrected before placement.

reference.reason: All parts and steps are correct, and the rear scratch and wall anchoring are out of scope. However, the 5 mm unloaded wobble exceeds the 4 mm limit, triggering the exception. The single accessible loose cam needs a straightforward tightening before retest, so level 2 applies.

legend.0: 0 — Unsafe or unusable: structural damage, severe instability, or an assembly error creates an immediate collapse or injury risk; stop use and disassemble or replace affected parts.
legend.1: 1 — Major correction required: missing or wrongly oriented structural parts, skipped steps, or multiple inaccessible fastening errors require parts sorting or substantial step correction before retesting.
legend.2: 2 — Minor correction required before placement: the build is otherwise complete and correctly assembled, but one or a few accessible fasteners need tightening, or unloaded wobble exceeds 4 mm; route to tightening and retest.
legend.3: 3 — Standard pass: all in-scope parts and steps are correct, accessible fasteners are secure, unloaded wobble is 4 mm or less, and only excluded matters such as rear-only cosmetic marks or pending wall anchoring remain.
legend.4: 4 — Excellent pass: meets level 3 and also has clean visible surfaces, consistently flush joints, even shelf alignment, and no observed wobble during the unloaded test.

criteria: 0 — Pass: Assembly matches the instructions, is stable, and needs no corrective action.
1 — Final placement: Assembly is correct and stable, but safe positioning, leveling, or clearance adjustment remains.
2 — Tightening: Correct parts and sequence were used, but loose installed hardware must be tightened.
3 — Step correction: All required parts are available, but an incorrect sequence, orientation, or connection must be undone and rebuilt.
4 — Parts sorting: A required component is missing, wrong, damaged, or mixed up and must be identified or replaced before rebuilding.
decision.instructions: Resolve references in the notes, compare the evidence with the supplied assembly sequence, and select exactly one indexed level. Apply the highest applicable level.

state.context: A household assembler built a fictional Larkspur wall cabinet in the living room. Inspection routes range from a clean pass to parts problems. When several conditions appear, use the highest applicable route.
evidence: Assembler’s note: “I installed the upper shelf before the rear crossbar. When I tried to add it, it would not fit, so I left it beside the cabinet.”
The parts checker counted every listed component and photographed the undamaged rear crossbar beside the cabinet; all installed screws were snug.
The instructions place the rear crossbar before the upper shelf. The final-use tester reports wobbling until that sequence is corrected.
state.request: Choose the inspection route and severity level.

reference.reason: In the assembler’s note, both instances of “it” refer to the rear crossbar, not the upper shelf. The crossbar is present and undamaged but could not be installed because the shelf was fitted out of sequence. reference.reason: The revision satisfies the Director’s structural condition by moving the whistle before the door shot. The only remaining brief violation is the missing eye-line arrow, a localized performance-notation fix that should be routed to the Storyboard artist and does not require a Writer rewrite or story re-review.

legend.0: 0 — Not viable: the sequence contradicts the core brief and needs replacement or extensive reconception before further review.
legend.1: 1 — Major revision required: multiple story or staging problems remain and the sequence must return to the Writer or Director for substantial changes and full re-review.
legend.2: 2 — Blocked pending creative decision: a substantive continuity or intent issue remains that cannot be fixed through straightforward board execution and requires Writer or Director resolution before advancing.
legend.3: 3 — Conditionally ready: the story condition is satisfied, but one localized, clearly specified board or performance fix must be completed by the relevant creative role before handoff; no story rethink is needed.
legend.4: 4 — Fully ready: the sequence meets all brief, continuity, staging, and notation requirements and can advance immediately without revision.

criteria: 0 — Not assessable: the current storyboard or essential brief is absent, so readiness cannot be checked and the package must not advance.

1 — Major rework required: the current version contradicts a core story or continuity requirement, or is too incomplete for meaningful handoff; route substantive revisions to the responsible creative roles.
2 — Significant revision required: the sequence is understandable but still has at least one unresolved brief requirement or multiple handoff defects; keep it out of layout and route specific notes.

3 — Conditionally ready: all core story and continuity requirements are met, but one minor, localized handoff defect remains that can be corrected without redesigning the sequence; advance only after that correction is verified.

4 — Fully ready: the latest version meets every stated story, continuity, panel-count, and camera-note requirement, and relevant role confirmations show no unresolved revisions; approve for layout with no further note routing.
decision.instructions: Select one readiness level. Later evidence supersedes earlier evidence when it explicitly replaces a prior version. Evaluate the current sequence against every stated brief and handoff requirement; older resolved notes must not lower the score.

state.context: The team is reviewing the rooftop escape sequence for the animated short “Paper Comet.” The brief requires readable left-to-right pursuit, Lina visibly choosing to rescue the trapped bird before escaping, and 24 numbered panels with camera notes before layout handoff.
evidence: At 09:00, Director Mara rejected version 2 because panel 15 reversed pursuit direction; Writer Sol noted Lina’s rescue choice was unclear; Animation producer Ivo found missing camera notes.

At 14:00, Storyboard artist Kez submitted version 3, explicitly replacing version 2. It has 24 numbered panels, maintains left-to-right pursuit, adds Lina spotting and turning toward the bird across panels 12–14, and includes camera notes on every panel.
At 15:00, Mara and Sol confirmed their narrative notes were resolved, and Ivo confirmed the package met layout-handoff requirements.
state.request: Using only the latest applicable evidence, rate the sequence’s readiness for layout and identify whether any further role-routed revision is required.

reference.reason: Version 3 explicitly replaces version 2 and satisfies all brief and technical requirements: pursuit direction is consistent, Lina’s rescue choice is clear, all 24 panels are numbered, and every panel has camera notes. The Director, Writer, and Animation producer each confirm resolution or handoff compliance, so no further role-routed revision is required.

criteria.design_hold_level3: Route to design, do not approve, and rate Level 3 because PDF clipping or layout hides part of the ordering code.
criteria.editorial_hold_level3: Route to editorial, do not approve, and rate Level 3 because the approved source copy contains wrong ordering information.
criteria.none_of_above: None of the listed combinations correctly states the required route, approval decision, and severity.
criteria.print_approve_level1: Route to print production, approve without holding the job, and rate Level 1 because the difference is purely cosmetic.
criteria.print_correct_level2: Route to print production, approve with a correction noted, and rate Level 2 because the printed defect remains usable.
criteria.publisher_stop_level4: Route to the catalog publisher, do not approve, and rate Level 4 because the issue is an unresolved legal or safety-critical contradiction.

decision.instructions: Choose the single option that correctly combines defect routing, yes/no approval, and severity. Route source-copy errors to editorial, PDF layout or clipping errors to design, and defects introduced between a correct PDF and paper output to print production. Use this ordered scale: Level 1 = cosmetic, approve; Level 2 = minor but usable, approve with correction noted; Level 3 = wrong ordering information, do not approve; Level 4 = legal or safety-critical contradiction, stop publication. Route to the publisher only when ownership or a policy waiver is unresolved.

input.state: At Northstar Editions, the production editor checks the press proof for a fictional sculpture catalog. The approved manuscript and signed print-ready PDF both show inventory code “PL-8427.” Reviewing the paper proof, the print coordinator reports that “the identifier arrives on paper one character short”; the same loss appears on two press sheets. The graphic designer confirms that the PDF has ample space around the full code and no clipping mask. Buyers use the code to place orders. The catalog publisher asks whether printing may proceed and which team must correct the defect.

reference.reason: “One character short” paraphrases the loss of the final digit from PL-8427. Because the manuscript and PDF are correct while two press sheets reproduce the loss, this is a print-production defect. It creates wrong ordering information, so the proof is Level 3 and must not be approved. No substantive option gives that exact combination.

criteria.readiness_1_print_rejection: Rate 1 and route primarily to the print coordinator: at least one reproduction tolerance is exceeded; this route takes precedence over simultaneous editorial or design defects.
criteria.readiness_2_editorial_hold: Rate 2 and route primarily to the production editor: all print specifications pass, but one or more text corrections are required.
criteria.readiness_3_approve: Rate 3 and send to the catalog publisher for final approval: every print specification passes and no text correction is required.

decision.instructions: Apply the stated ordered-scale rubric and its precedence rule. Select exactly one option using only the supplied evidence.

state.context: For the fictional Lumen Gallery catalog, the production editor checks text, the graphic designer owns layout files, the print coordinator owns reproduction tolerances, and the catalog publisher gives final approval. Readiness scale: 3—approve only if all print specifications are met and no text correction is needed; 2—hold with editorial only if print specifications are met but text needs correction; 1—reject and route to print production if any reproduction tolerance is exceeded, regardless of other defects.
evidence: The contract proof shows cyan misregistration of 0.45 mm on page 27; the supplied maximum is 0.30 mm.
The page 27 caption says “2025,” while the approved manuscript says “2026.”
Trim, pagination, image resolution, and all other checked specifications pass.
state.request: Choose the single readiness rating and primary route supported by the proof evidence.

reference.reason: The measured cyan misregistration is 0.45 mm, exceeding the 0.30 mm maximum. Under the precedence rule, any reproduction-tolerance breach requires rating 1 and routing to print production, despite the separate caption error.

criteria.false: No — do not withhold or route to editorial; approve the proof as readiness level 3 or 4.
criteria.true: Yes — withhold approval and route the proof to editorial for a missing or trim-violating artist credit.

decision.instructions: Verification task: Should the proof be withheld and routed to editorial because the page-31 artist credit is missing or violates the trim requirement? Use this ordered readiness scale: 1 = blocked by confirmed content or production defect; 2 = major correction needed; 3 = approvable with a minor nonblocking issue; 4 = fully ready. A measurement equal to a stated minimum passes. Approve proofs rated 3 or 4; withhold only those rated 1 or 2.

state.speaker: Production editor
state.text: The final bound proof is 64 pages. The artist credit on page 31 is not missing; it appears beneath the image as specified. All captions match the approved manuscript.

state.speaker: Graphic designer
state.text: The page-31 credit measures exactly 3.0 mm from the trim line. The specification requires text to be at least 3.0 mm inside trim, so it meets the limit.

state.speaker: Print coordinator
state.text: Registration, bleeds, and CMYK separations pass. Crop marks are absent, but the specification says they are not required on bound proofs.

state.speaker: Catalog publisher
state.text: Apply the readiness rubric and decide whether approval must be withheld for an editorial defect.

reference.reason: No. The credit is explicitly not missing, and its 3.0 mm trim distance exactly meets the minimum. The absent crop marks are also expressly permitted. The proof is readiness level 4, so no editorial hold is justified.

criteria.false: Do not route it to editorial at Level 3; instead classify it at another readiness level or grant final approval.
criteria.true: Route the spelling defect to the production editor and rate the proof Level 3, conditionally ready pending correction.

decision.instructions: Decide whether the proof should be routed to the production editor and rated Level 3—conditionally ready—rather than finally approved. Use this ordered readiness scale: Level 1 = blocked by critical defects; Level 2 = substantial design or production revisions required; Level 3 = technical checks pass and only minor editorial corrections remain; Level 4 = fully approved with no defects.

input.state: For the fictional North Quay Sculpture catalog, the print coordinator inspects the final proof. Specifications require every image to be at least 300 ppi and every page to have 3 mm bleed; the graphic designer confirms both requirements pass. The production editor finds one remaining defect: artist “Joan Miró” is printed as “Joan Miro” on page 27. The catalog publisher’s instruction is: “If technical specifications pass and the only open defect is copy-related, route it to editorial and classify the proof as conditionally ready, but do not grant final approval until corrected.” No other defects are recorded.

reference.reason: Yes. The image-resolution and bleed specifications pass, and the sole remaining issue is a minor copy defect. Under the publisher’s conditional instruction and the readiness rubric, it belongs with editorial at Level 3, not Level 4 final approval.

criteria: 0 — No current defect: the newest proof meets every supplied specification. Approve the proof; no routing is required.

1 — Minor current defect: an error remains but does not affect required dimensions, bleed, page presence, or factual text. Do not approve; route wording issues to Editorial or visual issues to Design.

2 — Major current defect: the newest proof violates trim, bleed, required page presence, or factual text specifications. Do not approve; route text/page-content defects to Editorial, layout defects to Design, and physical print-specification defects to Print Production.
decision.instructions: Use the latest-proof rule and select exactly one ordered severity level. Apply the approval and routing consequence stated in that level.

state.context: For the fictional Northlight Ceramics exhibition catalog, the Production editor and Graphic designer inspect proofs; the Print coordinator verifies press specifications, and the Catalog publisher grants final approval. Assess only the newest dated proof because each revision supersedes earlier evidence. Approval is allowed only when no current defect remains; any defect must be routed to its responsible team.
evidence: Specification: 210 × 280 mm trim, 3 mm bleed, pages 1–48 present, and artist name spelled “Mara Venn.”
September 14 proof: page 27 spelled the artist “Mara Ven” and lacked outer bleed; editorial and design corrections were requested.
September 16 replacement proof: page 27 now reads “Mara Venn,” measures 3 mm outer bleed, matches trim size, and all 48 pages are present.
state.request: Rate the current proof’s defect severity, state whether it is approved, and identify any required routing under the rubric.

reference.reason: The September 16 replacement proof supersedes the September 14 proof and verifies that both earlier defects were corrected. It also meets trim, bleed, spelling, and page-count specifications. Therefore no current defect remains, no team routing is required, and the proof is approved.

legend.0: 0 — No current defect: the newest proof meets every supplied specification. Approve the proof; no routing is required.
legend.1: 1 — Minor current defect: an error remains but does not affect required dimensions, bleed, page presence, or factual text. Do not approve; route wording issues to Editorial or visual issues to Design.
legend.2: 2 — Major current defect: the newest proof violates trim, bleed, required page presence, or factual text specifications. Do not approve; route text/page-content defects to Editorial, layout defects to Design, and physical print-specification defects to Print Production.

criteria: 0 — Approve: No verified specification or content defects remain; the catalog may proceed to print without changes.
1 — Conditional hold: Exactly one localized, correctable defect is verified, affects only one team, and requires a targeted correction plus reproof before printing.

2 — Reject for major revision: Any factual/content-integrity defect, structural or trim-risk defect, or two or more verified defects require broader correction or coordination across teams before a new full proof.
decision.instructions: Decide the proof’s readiness using the ordered scale. Apply specification thresholds strictly, even when the miss is small or not visually obvious. A single image-resolution defect is routed to graphic design for replacement or resampling; editorial handles text/content defects, and print production handles bleed, color-bar, imposition, or press-file defects.

state.speaker: Production editor
state.text: The 96-page Lumen Chairs catalog proof has correct captions, prices, pagination, and contents links. Editorial found no text defects.

state.speaker: Graphic designer
state.text: My layout panel reports the full-page chair image on page 41 at 300 effective ppi, and the printed proof looks clean. I recommend approval.

state.speaker: Print coordinator
state.text: The printer’s RIP report for the supplied press PDF records that image at 218 ppi. The catalog specification requires at least 225 ppi. All other images, bleeds, and color bars pass.

state.speaker: Catalog publisher
state.text: Apply the readiness rubric and route any verified defect. When layout data conflicts with the RIP report, our policy treats the RIP report as authoritative for the file actually being printed.

reference.reason: The authoritative RIP report shows 218 ppi, below the strict 225 ppi minimum. Despite the designer’s conflicting 300-ppi reading and the clean appearance, this is one localized, design-owned defect; all other checks pass. Approval should therefore be held only until correction and reproof.

legend.0: 0 — Approve: No verified specification or content defects remain; the catalog may proceed to print without changes.
legend.1: 1 — Conditional hold: Exactly one localized, correctable defect is verified, affects only one team, and requires a targeted correction plus reproof before printing.
legend.2: 2 — Reject for major revision: Any factual/content-integrity defect, structural or trim-risk defect, or two or more verified defects require broader correction or coordination across teams before a new full proof.

criteria.insufficient_evidence_hold: Place on evidence hold: the record neither proves a core violation nor supplies enough explicit documentation to confirm all core requirements or a claimed sensor exception.
criteria.invalid_protocol_failure: Route for protocol failure: explicit evidence shows nonrandom assignment, unequal pre-trial watering, an uncovered watering event, missing final growth measurements, or another violated core requirement.
criteria.valid_documented_exception: Accept as treatment-control valid and route to analysis: every core requirement is explicitly supported, and any sensor gap is fully covered by qualifying dated manual records.

decision.instructions: Select exactly one routing option. Apply the explicit protocol rule: all core requirements must be evidenced; a sensor gap is acceptable only if independently documented manual records cover every affected watering event.

state.context: A data quality reviewer is triaging a fictional tomato drought trial run by a greenhouse technician and overseen by a plant ecologist. The protocol requires randomized treatment assignment, identical pre-trial watering, drought-pot watering records, and final growth measurements. One missing sensor stream is allowed only when dated manual records independently document every affected watering event.
evidence: The signed randomization sheet assigns benches 1 and 3 to drought and benches 2 and 4 to control before treatment began.
Technician logs show all pots received 300 mL daily for seven pre-trial days.
The flow sensor for drought bench 3 failed on days 4–6; dated manual logs record 100 mL for every pot on each affected day and bear both actors’ initials.
Final dry-mass measurements are present for all 48 plants, with calibrated-scale identifiers.
state.request: Classify the trial’s treatment-control validity under the stated protocol and route it accordingly.

reference.reason: The trial has explicit evidence of prior randomization, uniform pre-trial watering, complete watering documentation, and final measurements. Although one sensor stream failed, dated manual records cover every affected event and are jointly initialed, satisfying the protocol’s allowed exception.

criteria.invalid_documented_crossover: INVALID: At least one tray received the watering schedule assigned to the opposite group.
criteria.provisional_minor_data_gap: PROVISIONAL: No crossover, but sensor completeness is 80% to below 90%, or exactly one endpoint is missing.
criteria.unverifiable_or_severely_incomplete: UNVERIFIABLE: Evidence does not establish whether crossover occurred, or sensor completeness is below 80%.
criteria.valid_at_threshold: VALID: Assignment and absence of crossover are documented, sensor completeness is at least 90%, and every endpoint is present.

decision.instructions: Verify treatment-control validity using this rubric: VALID requires documented assignment, evidence of no watering crossover, at least 90% sensor completeness, and all endpoint measurements. PROVISIONAL requires no crossover but 80% to below 90% sensor completeness or one missing endpoint. INVALID applies when any watering crossover is documented. UNVERIFIABLE applies when crossover status lacks evidence or sensor completeness is below 80%. Select exactly one option.

state.speaker: plant ecologist
state.text: Twenty bean trays were randomized before watering: ten drought-treatment and ten controls. The trial required daily soil-moisture readings for 10 days, plus final height and biomass for every tray.

state.speaker: greenhouse technician
state.text: The signed watering ledger shows all treatment trays received the assigned drought pulses. No control tray received a drought pulse; each control followed the standard schedule.

state.speaker: data quality reviewer
state.text: I count 180 of 200 required moisture readings. Final height and biomass are present for all 20 trays. There are no duplicate tray IDs.

state.speaker: plant ecologist
state.text: So moisture completeness is exactly 90%, not below it, and the ledger supports absence of treatment crossover.

reference.reason: The signed ledger explicitly establishes that no control received drought treatment, while all treatment trays followed their assignment. Sensor completeness is exactly 90%, which meets the inclusive threshold, and all endpoints are present.

criteria.false: Tray B was not protocol-intended for drought because at least one required condition failed, activating the daily-watering fallback.
criteria.true: Tray B was protocol-intended for drought because every required condition in the ecologist’s conditional assignment was satisfied.

decision.instructions: Verification task: Decide whether tray B was protocol-intended for drought treatment. Answer yes only if the stated calibration condition for drought assignment was satisfied before watering began. Complete growth measurements do not substitute for satisfying the assignment condition.

input.state: Before the drought trial, plant ecologist Mira documented: “If all four soil-moisture sensors pass the 08:00 calibration, assign tray B to drought and tray A to daily watering; otherwise water both trays daily as controls.” At 08:00, three sensors passed, but B-4 failed. Greenhouse technician Leon nevertheless withheld water from tray B for four days and watered tray A daily. Heights were measured each morning, and the data quality reviewer confirmed that the growth records were complete. The reviewer must now determine whether tray B’s drought treatment reflects the documented assignment intent.

reference.reason: No. The documented intent assigned tray B to drought only if all four sensors passed calibration, but sensor B-4 failed. The fallback intent was to water both trays daily, so the technician’s withholding did not reflect the protocol-intended assignment.

criteria.false: No — do not route the trial as ready because at least one assignment, watering, or measurement-coverage condition is violated or unsupported.
criteria.true: Yes — route the trial as ready for treatment-effect analysis because all stated validity and data-coverage conditions are satisfied.

decision.instructions: Answer yes if the evidence establishes compliant assignment timing, watering, and required measurement coverage after applying the temporal-update rule. Answer no if any readiness condition remains unsupported or violated.

state.context: A plant ecologist asks whether a fictional tomato drought trial is ready for treatment-effect analysis. Protocol: baseline height must precede random assignment; watering must stay within ±10 mL; one sensor gap is acceptable if every scheduled reading has a gravimetric backup. A later signed correction supersedes an earlier unsigned entry when supported by an instrument audit.
evidence: The greenhouse technician’s unsigned 11 May note lists baseline height at 09:00 and randomization at 08:40.
On 12 May, the technician signed a correction: randomization occurred at 09:20; the controller audit records the assignment command at 09:20:14.
Drought and control watering records stayed within ±6 mL. A 14 May moisture-sensor gap has gravimetric backups for every scheduled reading, and final heights are recorded.
The data quality reviewer verified the controller audit, backup weights, and growth table on 15 May.
state.request: Under the stated protocol and update rule, is the trial ready for treatment-effect analysis?

reference.reason: The signed 12 May correction, corroborated by the controller audit, supersedes the earlier unsigned timing entry and shows baseline measurement preceded randomization. Watering stayed within tolerance, the sensor gap is fully backed up, final growth measurements exist, and the reviewer verified the records.

criteria: 0 — Not validatable: At least one analyzed pot has unresolved conflicting primary assignment records, or no primary assignment evidence exists; treatment-control comparisons cannot be accepted.

1 — Weak validity: Primary assignment records are consistent, but a documented protocol deviation or missing watering record affects at least one analyzed pot without making assignment identity ambiguous.
2 — Adequate validity: Primary assignments are consistent and all analyzed pots have complete watering records; minor non-assignment metadata or growth-measurement issues are documented and bounded.

3 — Strong validity: Primary assignments are consistent and independently reconciled, watering and sensor records are complete, all growth measurements pass quality checks, and no material protocol deviations remain.
decision.instructions: Rate the treatment-control validity of DR-18 as submitted. Apply the levels in order from low to high. Assignment identity must be established independently of observed watering. An unresolved contradiction between primary assignment records for any analyzed pot requires level 0, even when sensor records support one record.

state.speaker: greenhouse technician
state.text: Trial DR-18 used 12 tomato pots. The signed bench map assigns P07 to drought and P08 to control; watering logs follow that map.

state.speaker: plant ecologist
state.text: The RFID assignment export created before treatment onset instead lists P07 as control and P08 as drought. I believe tags were swapped physically, but I did not record a correction.

state.speaker: data quality reviewer
state.text: Both the signed map and timestamped RFID export are designated primary assignment records. Sensor data show P07 received 180 mL and P08 received 420 mL per cycle, consistent with the map, but watering volume does not establish label identity.

state.speaker: plant ecologist
state.text: The final growth analysis includes both P07 and P08 under the bench-map labels; neither pot was excluded.

reference.reason: The signed bench map and timestamped RFID export conflict over the treatment identities of analyzed pots P07 and P08, and no documented correction resolves the contradiction. The watering data cannot independently prove assignment identity under the rubric, so level 0 is required.

legend.0: 0 — Not validatable: At least one analyzed pot has unresolved conflicting primary assignment records, or no primary assignment evidence exists; treatment-control comparisons cannot be accepted.
legend.1: 1 — Weak validity: Primary assignment records are consistent, but a documented protocol deviation or missing watering record affects at least one analyzed pot without making assignment identity ambiguous.
legend.2: 2 — Adequate validity: Primary assignments are consistent and all analyzed pots have complete watering records; minor non-assignment metadata or growth-measurement issues are documented and bounded.
legend.3: 3 — Strong validity: Primary assignments are consistent and independently reconciled, watering and sensor records are complete, all growth measurements pass quality checks, and no material protocol deviations remain.

criteria: 0 — Unusable: Treatment identities or outcome measurements are missing, so no treatment-control comparison can be evaluated.
1 — Limited: Treatment identities and outcomes are recorded, but at least one critical assignment or protocol record is missing, preventing verification of treatment-control validity.
2 — Adequate: All critical assignment, watering, sensor, and outcome records are available; only a noncritical supporting detail is missing.
3 — Complete: All critical records and supporting documentation are available, internally consistent, timestamped, and sufficient to reconstruct assignment and protocol execution.
decision.instructions: Rate the completeness of the available evidence for evaluating whether the drought and control groups were validly assigned. Use the ordered rubric below and select one level.

input.state: A greenhouse technician reports a 21-day trial of 24 tomato seedlings: 12 labeled drought received 80 mL every four days, while 12 labeled control received 80 mL daily. Soil-moisture sensors have timestamped records for all pots, and baseline and final heights are recorded. However, the treatment-assignment sheet and original bench map are missing. The plant ecologist therefore cannot verify how seedlings were allocated, whether assignment occurred before baseline measurement, or whether initial plant size influenced group placement. A data quality reviewer must rate the evidence completeness for evaluating treatment-control validity.

reference.reason: Watering, sensor, and growth records are present, but the missing assignment sheet and bench map prevent verification of unbiased treatment allocation. Under the rubric, this is limited evidence with a critical record missing.

legend.0: 0 — Unusable: Treatment identities or outcome measurements are missing, so no treatment-control comparison can be evaluated.
legend.1: 1 — Limited: Treatment identities and outcomes are recorded, but at least one critical assignment or protocol record is missing, preventing verification of treatment-control validity.
legend.2: 2 — Adequate: All critical assignment, watering, sensor, and outcome records are available; only a noncritical supporting detail is missing.
legend.3: 3 — Complete: All critical records and supporting documentation are available, internally consistent, timestamped, and sufficient to reconstruct assignment and protocol execution.

criteria.data_review_yes_low: Completeness Yes; Data-review queue; Low confidence. Choose only if a record contradiction remains after correction precedence is applied and a needed routing fact conflicts.
criteria.identification_yes_high: Completeness Yes; Identification queue; High confidence. Choose only if the complete record has no remaining contradiction, at least one taxon is explicitly unresolved, and all routing facts are direct and consistent.
criteria.sampling_no_medium: Completeness No; Sampling queue; Medium confidence. Choose only if at least one required completeness element is absent and that conclusion requires one inference.
criteria.validated_yes_medium: Completeness Yes; Validated; Medium confidence. Choose only if no contradiction or unresolved taxon remains and one required routing fact must be inferred.

decision.instructions: Select the combined completeness judgment, queue, and confidence rating. Completeness is Yes only when effort is at least 30 minutes, the site label exactly matches the register, every specimen lot has a numeric count, and all four habitat observations are present. Route incomplete surveys to Sampling; otherwise route remaining record contradictions to Data Review; otherwise route any unresolved taxon to Identification; otherwise mark Validated. A later explicit statement that an identification is not confirmed controls over its quoted tentative note and is not itself a contradiction. Confidence is ordered High > Medium > Low: High requires all routing facts to be explicit and consistent; Medium requires one inference; Low means a needed fact conflicts.

state.speaker: field survey lead
state.text: Survey D247 covered registered site ST-08 for exactly 30 minutes; the field-sheet label is ST-08. We collected three specimen lots.

state.speaker: ecology data manager
state.text: All lots have numeric counts: stonefly 12, caddisfly 7, and mayfly 6. Flow, substrate, canopy shade, and wetted width are all recorded.

state.speaker: taxonomic identifier
state.text: Voucher V4 is not identified to species. “Baetis tricaudatus” was only my tentative note, so the mayfly remains unresolved.

state.speaker: watershed coordinator
state.text: The site register confirms ST-08, and there are no other edits or conflicting records.

reference.reason: The survey is complete because 30 minutes meets the inclusive effort threshold, the ST-08 label matches, all counts are numeric, and all four habitat observations are present. The identifier explicitly says V4 is not identified and remains unresolved; the tentative species note does not override that negation. With no remaining contradiction, the case routes to Identification at High confidence.

criteria.data_review_count_mismatch: Route to the ecology data manager when all vial codes are logged but the field-sheet and custody-record specimen totals disagree.
criteria.identification_all_records_complete: Route to the taxonomic identifier when all six vial codes appear in the transfer log and effort, counts, and habitat records are complete.
criteria.none_of_above: Choose when the evidence requires a queue-and-condition combination not represented by any substantive option.
criteria.sampling_effort_incomplete: Route to the sampling queue when incomplete required sampling effort is the sole relevant deficiency.
criteria.watershed_habitat_missing: Route to the watershed coordinator when habitat observations are missing but vial transfer, effort, and specimen-count records are complete.

decision.instructions: Select the option whose queue and evidence profile exactly match the survey. The profiles are mutually exclusive: each substantive option applies only when its stated condition is the sole relevant condition. Apply the field survey lead’s conditional routing intent to the supplied records. If the matching queue-and-condition profile is not offered, choose none_of_above.

input.state: Field survey lead Mara submits Pine Fork surveys for sites PF-1 and PF-2. Each site received the required 15-minute kick sample and 5-minute hand search. All six vials have legible site codes, specimen counts total 47 on both the field sheets and custody record, and flow, substrate, canopy, and temperature observations are complete. However, the transfer log lists only five vial codes; PF-2-C is absent. Mara states: “If every vial code appears in the transfer log, send the survey to taxonomic identification. If any code is absent, send it to data review. Do not order more sampling.”

reference.reason: PF-2-C is absent from the transfer log, so Mara’s explicit condition requires the data-review queue. The offered data-review option applies only to a specimen-count mismatch, but both records total 47. Sampling effort and habitat observations are complete, so no substantive option matches.

criteria.false: No — at least one completeness requirement fails under the latest information, so ST-41 is not ready and must be routed according to the stated rule.
criteria.true: Yes — all required effort, labeling, counts, identifications, and habitat records reconcile under the latest information, so ST-41 is ready for acceptance.

decision.instructions: Answer yes only if every completeness requirement remains satisfied after applying temporal updates. Otherwise answer no. Base confidence on the ordered definitions in the request.

state.context: A field survey lead submitted site ST-41 as complete: six timed kick samples, 18 specimens, labeled vials, and habitat observations for flow, substrate, canopy, and bank condition. The taxonomic identifier recorded 18 identifications, and the ecology data manager initially reconciled them. Two days later, the watershed coordinator issued a controlling correction: vial 6, containing three specimens, was collected at ST-14, not ST-41. No revised ST-41 specimen total or identification sheet has been supplied.
evidence: Completeness requires documented effort, correct site labels, reconciled specimen counts and identifications, and all four habitat observations.
Use the latest dated correction over earlier records.
Any unresolved site/count mismatch makes the survey incomplete and routes it to data review; missing sampling effort would instead route to sampling, and unresolved species names to identification.
state.request: Is ST-41 complete and ready for acceptance? Also select confidence: High when the rule and decisive record are explicit; Medium when interpretation is needed; Low when required records are absent.

reference.reason: The later controlling correction moves three specimens from ST-41 to ST-14, leaving ST-41’s reported total of 18 and its identification sheet unreconciled. Under the explicit rubric, that mismatch makes the survey incomplete and routes it to data review. Confidence is High because both the update rule and consequence are explicit.

criteria.false: No — route to data review because a required field is missing or the specimen-count conflict remains unresolved.

The protocol identifies extraction volume as critical for comparing enzyme activity. No observation confirms that an incorrect volume was used, and neither operator nor scientist remembers it.

reference.reason: Setup and incubation are documented as compliant, while the extraction volume is missing rather than confirmed incorrect. Therefore, no substantive deviation route is supported.

criteria.true: Yes — the experiment qualifies as an acceptable protocol-compliant replication.

state.context: A soil scientist is reviewing a technician’s 14-day moisture microcosm replication. An instrument operator supplied the chamber log, and a replication reviewer must verify protocol compliance.
evidence: The protocol covers 14-day moisture microcosms and requires 60±2% water-holding capacity, 20±1°C incubation, and CO₂ measurements on days 3, 7, and 14.

Incubation exception: one shared temperature excursion may be accepted only if it lasts no more than 90 consecutive minutes and affects every treatment and paired control. Any longer excursion fails replication, regardless of shared exposure.
All jars began at 61% water-holding capacity, and all required CO₂ measurements were recorded.
The logger recorded 21.4°C from 10:05 to 11:40—95 consecutive minutes—across all treatments and controls.
state.request: Does this experiment qualify as an acceptable replication under the stated protocol?

reference.reason: The 95-minute temperature excursion exceeds the exception’s 90-minute maximum. Shared exposure does not rescue a longer excursion, so the incubation requirement fails.

criteria.false: No — do not route the case as an incubation issue.
criteria.true: Yes — route the case as an incubation issue.

decision.instructions: Using the stated routing rubric and the dialogue’s coreferences, decide whether this case should be routed as an incubation issue.

state.speaker: soil scientist
state.text: In the decomposition trial, sealed test jar Cedar and balance-check jar Elm began at 60% water-holding capacity. Elm is excluded from replication judgments.

state.speaker: microcosm technician
state.text: On day 2, Cedar read 48% and Elm 47%. I corrected the former exactly 72 hours after its first low reading; the latter was corrected within 6 hours.

state.speaker: instrument operator
state.text: Independent gravimetric checks confirmed both moisture readings, and the moisture probe passed calibration before and after incubation.

state.speaker: replication reviewer
state.text: Route as an incubation issue when a sealed test jar remains outside 55–65% for at least 72 hours; exactly 72 qualifies. Ignore excluded jars. Setup and measurement issues take precedence only when sealing or instrument checks fail.

reference.reason: Yes. “The former” refers to Cedar, the sealed test jar. Cedar remained below the allowed moisture range for exactly 72 hours, which explicitly meets the inclusive incubation threshold; instrument and sealing failures are absent.

criteria: 0 — Not reproducible: setup, incubation, or measurement information is largely absent, so protocol compliance cannot be assessed.
1 — Poor control: records exist, but at least one major required element is missing or substantially wrong, such as jar count, soil mass, moisture treatment, incubation duration, or CO₂ measurement.

input.state: A soil scientist’s protocol requires twelve identical 500-mL jars, each with 200 g of homogenized soil, six adjusted to 20% moisture and six to 35%, incubated at 25°C for 14 days with vented lids. On day 14, an instrument operator calibrated the CO₂ analyzer with the specified standard and measured every jar once. The soil came in brown bags, jar labels were blue, and the incubator stood on the lower shelf; none of these details is specified by the protocol. The replication reviewer finds complete setup, incubation, calibration, and measurement records.

reference.reason: All required setup, moisture groups, incubation conditions, duration, calibration, measurements, and records match the protocol. The bag color, label color, and shelf position are explicitly non-required distractors.
