decision.instructions: Rate replication completeness using the five ordered levels. Interpret paraphrased observations by whether they satisfy the protocol’s substantive requirements, not by matching wording. A core treatment is identifiable only when records establish that the intended moisture levels were actually set.

state.context: A soil scientist’s protocol tests moisture effects on decomposition in 12 sealed soil microcosms, with four independent jars per treatment. The replication reviewer must rate experimental-control completeness from the records.
evidence: Protocol: determine each jar’s oven-dry soil mass and water-holding capacity, then adjust separately to 30%, 60%, or 90% capacity before incubation at 20°C.

The microcosm technician recorded adding the same 12 mL to every jar containing 100 g of field-moist soil; dampness was judged by squeezing, without drying subsamples or measuring water-holding capacity.
The instrument operator calibrated the CO₂ analyzer, measured each jar separately, and retained all raw files. Treatment labels and incubation temperature were preserved.
state.request: Assign the ordered completeness level and decide whether this counts as a valid replication.

reference.reason: The technician’s equal-volume, squeeze-tested dosing does not establish jar-specific dry mass or water-holding capacity, so the intended moisture treatments cannot be identified. Later calibrated measurements cannot repair that core setup failure; the replication is rejected.

criteria: Level 0 — Receive normally: PO, ASN, labels, count, and inspection all agree, with no discrepancy requiring follow-up.

Level 1 — Routine receiving correction: a minor clerical or carton-level variance is fully resolved by supplied documents, with item identity and authorization confirmed; receive stock and log the correction.

Level 2 — Quarantine and route to Inventory Control: quantity is usable and no immediate operational interruption exists, but evidence shows a wrong revision, wrong item, or undocumented substitution lacking required buyer approval; block inventory pending verification.

Level 3 — Escalate to Dock Supervisor and Supplier Claims: evidence shows safety-critical mismatch, widespread damage, material shortage, or wrong goods likely to stop operations; reject or hold the load and open a supplier claim immediately.
decision.instructions: Assign the shipment to exactly one ordered discrepancy level using only the explicit evidence. Apply the highest level whose conditions are supported. This is a routing-and-severity decision; an undocumented revision substitution is not cleared merely by passing inspection or by a supplier's equivalence claim.

criteria.expedite_purchase_south: Choose only if monitoring and transfer fail, and the expedited order arrives by day 3 and leaves South with nonnegative net stock.
criteria.insufficient_data: Choose only if the supplied balances, timing, quantities, demand, or coreference information is insufficient to apply the routing rules.
criteria.monitor_or_allocate_local: Choose only if South can cover its demand snapshot and the additional request from available local stock while remaining at or above its reorder point.
criteria.shortage_escalation: Choose only if local stock, transfer, expedite, and standard purchase all fail to cover the requirement by its due date.
criteria.standard_purchase_south: Choose only if monitoring and transfer fail, no qualifying expedite route applies, and the standard purchase arrives by day 3 with nonnegative South net.
criteria.transfer_north_to_south: Choose if monitoring fails and the fixed North-to-South transfer is timely, leaves South nonnegative, and leaves North at or above its reorder point.

decision.instructions: Route the requirement using the first matching rule. Available stock equals on-hand minus reservations. Monitor/local allocation applies if South’s available stock minus its snapshot and request remains at or above its reorder point. Otherwise transfer if it arrives by day 3, South’s resulting 7-day net is nonnegative, and North’s available stock minus its demand and transfer remains at or above North’s reorder point; equality qualifies. Otherwise expedite, then standard-purchase, if the respective receipt is timely and makes South’s net nonnegative. Route to shortage escalation if no timely method covers it; choose insufficient data only if calculation is impossible. Resolve the requester’s coreferences when identifying the destination and quantity.

state.speaker: Internal materials requester
state.text: I need 10 units within 3 days. Please deliver them to that depot; those are additional to its demand snapshot.

state.speaker: Distribution center manager
state.text: North-to-South transfer time is 2 days with a fixed 15-unit quantity. A standard South purchase is 30 units in 6 days; an expedited South order is 20 units in 3 days.

reference.reason: “That depot” refers to South, and “those” refers to the additional 10 units. Local net is 35−20−18−10 = −13, so monitoring fails. A 15-unit transfer arrives in 2 days, leaves South at 2 units net, and leaves North at 137−70−12−15 = 40, exactly its reorder point; equality qualifies.

criteria.inter_dc_transfer: Route to an inter-DC transfer only when the source has stock above its own reorder point after reservations and the 3-day transfer arrives before the confirmed demand date.
criteria.none_of_above: Choose when neither substantive workflow meets policy; here, route to supplier expedite because confirmed demand is due before both transfer and standard-purchase arrival.
criteria.standard_purchase: Route to standard purchase only when net available stock is below the reorder point and no confirmed demand is due before the 7-day standard delivery.

decision.instructions: Select the correct replenishment workflow using the stated balances, timing, and routing policy.

input.state: At fictional Northgate DC, the distribution center manager reports 90 valve kits on hand and 35 reserved for an internal materials requester, leaving 55 net available. The reorder point is 60, and the fixed replenishment quantity is 100. The demand planner confirms 70 kits are required in 2 days. Eastbay DC has 180 on hand, 40 reserved, and a local reorder point of 100; a transfer takes 3 days. Standard purchase lead time is 7 days, while supplier expediting takes 1 day. Policy: purchase when net stock is below reorder point but no demand is due before standard delivery; transfer when surplus exists and arrives before demand; expedite when demand precedes both transfer and standard delivery. A pending packaging redesign next month is unrelated.

reference.reason: Northgate is below its reorder point, and the 70-kit demand is due in 2 days. Eastbay has transferable surplus, but its 3-day transfer would arrive too late; a standard purchase would also arrive too late at 7 days. Policy therefore requires the 1-day expedite workflow, which is not one of the substantive options. The packaging redesign is a distractor.

criteria.false: No — do not route it to transfer; at least one required condition fails, so use the expedited-purchase workflow.
criteria.true: Yes — route the proposed 20-unit movement from West to the transfer workflow because every transfer condition is satisfied.

decision.instructions: Answer yes or no using the stated routing policy. Treat “borrowing stock from West” as a paraphrase of an inventory transfer, and apply all three transfer conditions, including boundary equality at the donor’s reorder point.

state.context: A replenishment planner reviews fictional SKU AX-14 for the East and West depots. Policy defines available stock as on-hand minus reservations. Route to transfer only if East is below its reorder point, West will remain at or above its own reorder point after shipment, and the shipment will arrive no later than East’s projected stockout. Otherwise, route to expedited purchase.
evidence: East: 34 on hand, 10 reserved, reorder point 30, projected stockout in 3 days.
West: 90 on hand, 20 reserved, reorder point 50.
The internal materials requester proposes borrowing 20 units from West; depot-to-depot transit is 4 days.
state.request: Should the planner route the proposed borrowing of stock to the transfer workflow?

reference.reason: No. East is below its reorder point (24 available versus 30), and West would remain exactly at its reorder point (90−20−20=50), but the paraphrased transfer would arrive in 4 days, after East’s projected stockout in 3 days. The policy therefore routes this case to expedited purchase.

criteria.false: No — do not use expedited transfer; route to purchase or monitor because at least one stated policy test is not satisfied.
criteria.true: Yes — route the full 60-unit quantity to an expedited transfer from West to East because both inclusive threshold tests are satisfied.

decision.instructions: Should the 60-unit replenishment be routed to the expedited inter-DC transfer workflow? Answer yes or no using the stated balances, demand, transfer time, and inclusive policy thresholds.

state.speaker: Internal materials requester
state.text: East DC needs 60 units of part NX-4. Its on-hand balance is 120 units, with 30 reserved.

state.speaker: Demand planner
state.text: East demand is 20 units per day. West-to-East expedited transfer time is 2 days; no receipts are scheduled.

state.speaker: Distribution center manager
state.text: West has 240 units on hand and 40 reserved. Sending 60 would leave 140 available units. West’s reorder point is 140; East’s is 50.

state.speaker: Replenishment planner
state.text: Policy: expedite the full transfer when East’s available stock minus transfer-time demand is at or below its reorder point and West’s post-transfer available stock is at or above its reorder point. If either test fails, route to purchase; if East is above its reorder point, monitor.

reference.reason: Yes. East has 120 − 30 = 90 available units; after two days of demand, it will have 90 − (20 × 2) = 50, exactly its reorder point and therefore qualifying under “at or below.” West would retain 240 − 40 − 60 = 140 available units, exactly its reorder point and therefore satisfying “at or above.”

criteria: Level 0 — Monitor: Projected free stock is at or above the location’s reorder point, so no replenishment action is opened.

Level 1 — Routine purchase: Projected free stock is positive but below the reorder point, and no other location can transfer enough stock within three days without falling below its own reorder point; open a normal purchase workflow.

Level 2 — Standard transfer: Projected free stock is positive but below the reorder point, and another location can transfer at least the shortage amount within three days while remaining at or above its own reorder point.
Level 3 — Expedited transfer: Projected free stock is zero or negative, depletion is expected after 24 hours, and donor stock exists but requires an expedited transfer to arrive within three days.

Level 4 — Emergency allocation: Projected free stock is zero or negative within 24 hours, and neither a purchase nor a transfer can arrive within 24 hours; immediately ration or reallocate available inventory.
decision.instructions: Select the appropriate replenishment workflow. The five levels are ordered from lowest to highest shortage risk and intervention intensity. Apply the level definitions exactly to the stated projected free stock and source availability.

input.state: Replenishment planner Lina reviews West Depot with the distribution center manager. On-hand stock is 420 units. An internal materials requester’s reservation for 260 units has not been canceled and remains active. The demand planner forecasts another 110 units of demand over seven days. West’s reorder point is 100 units. A 200-unit purchase order arrives in 12 days. East Depot holds 80 units above its own reorder point; a standard transfer takes two days and uses a fixed 60-unit quantity. Policy calculates projected free stock as on-hand minus active reservations minus seven-day demand.

reference.reason: The reservation remains active despite the negation wording, so projected free stock is 420 − 260 − 110 = 50 units, which is positive but 50 below the 100-unit reorder point. East can send the fixed 60-unit quantity within two days while remaining above its own reorder point, so a standard transfer is justified.

criteria: No action: No credible requirement exists, or current destination stock covers all firm demand while remaining at or above its reorder point.
Monitor: A possible requirement exists, but it is not conditional on a pending event and no replenishment threshold will be breached before the next review.
Prepare transfer: Demand depends on an event that has not yet been confirmed; identify source stock and reserve transfer capacity, but do not release inventory.

Execute transfer: The condition has been confirmed, destination coverage is insufficient without action, and an available transfer arrives on time while leaving both locations at or above reorder points.
Expedite external supply: The requirement is confirmed, but no feasible transfer can arrive on time or preserve the source reorder point, so premium external replenishment is required.
decision.instructions: Choose one ordered intervention level. Use the lowest level that fully addresses the confirmed requirement while preserving both locations at or above their reorder points.

state.context: North DC has 115 units on hand, 60 reserved, and a 60-unit reorder point. South DC has 170 on hand, 20 reserved, and a 70-unit reorder point. The fixed transfer quantity is 50 units and transit time is one day. A standard 100-unit purchase takes seven days.
evidence: The internal materials requester needs 40 units at North in three days, but only if production batch K is released.

The South distribution center manager confirms 50 units can ship today. After transfer and demand, North would have 65 unreserved units; South would have 100.
state.request: As replenishment planner, assign the appropriate intervention level under the supplied rubric.

A one-day transfer arrives before the three-day need and leaves North at 65 and South at 100, both above reorder points. Therefore, execute the transfer; external expediting is unjustified.

criteria.none_of_above: Select when the line cannot be released and the evidence does not meet the materials-support rubric, including when an unresolved quality or maintenance requirement is the blocker.
criteria.release_to_production: Release the line to production only if every required readiness condition is satisfied, including a passed post-clean quality check.
criteria.route_to_materials_support: Do not release; route to materials support only if the sole blocker is material required for the currently scheduled Mint-500 run.

decision.instructions: Choose the single applicable routing/readiness outcome. Release requires current-job materials, approved tooling, completed cleaning records, adequate staffing, passed quality checks, and no open maintenance fault. Route to materials support only when the sole release blocker is missing or deficient material for the scheduled job.

input.state: The production scheduler plans Line 4’s changeover from Citrus-500 to Mint-500 at 14:00. Current-job bottles, caps, labels, and concentrate are staged in full; a shortage of blue caps affects only next week’s Ocean-750 run. The line supervisor confirms four trained operators and the approved Mint tooling installed. The maintenance technician closed yesterday’s conveyor sensor repair after a successful test; a worn spare guide remains tagged out in storage. Cleaning records show the required rinse completed, but the quality inspector reports that the mandatory post-clean allergen swab result is still pending. No other maintenance, staffing, tooling, or material issues are open.

reference.reason: Production release is not allowed because the mandatory allergen swab has not passed; its result is pending. Materials support is also incorrect because all materials for the scheduled Mint-500 run are staged. The blue-cap shortage and worn spare guide concern unrelated or inactive items.

criteria.maintenance_hold_high: Do not release; route to maintenance with high delay risk because tooling, guarding, sensors, or maintenance clearance remain open.
criteria.materials_hold_moderate: Do not release; route to materials support with moderate delay risk because ingredients, packaging, or lot verification are incomplete.
criteria.production_release_low: Release the line to production with low delay risk because every required gate is documented.
criteria.quality_hold_critical: Do not release; route to Quality with critical delay risk because cleaning verification or formal quality approval is missing.

decision.instructions: Select exactly one option. Apply this ordered scale: low risk means every release gate is documented; moderate means only materials are incomplete; high means an open tooling or maintenance gate; critical means required cleaning verification or quality approval is missing. A paraphrased readiness claim does not satisfy a source-record requirement.

state.context: At 13:10, the quality inspector reviews Line 4 for a 14:00 changeover from vanilla to allergen-free cereal. Plant policy requires materials, tooling, cleaning verification, minimum staffing, and quality signoff before release. A supervisor’s summary says, “Sanitation is finished and Quality approved the line.” Summaries are paraphrases only and cannot replace missing source records.
evidence: All scheduled ingredients and packaging are staged with matching lot numbers.
Tooling T-44 is installed; its torque check passed, and maintenance closed the guard-sensor note.
Five qualified operators are assigned, meeting the minimum of four.
The cleaning log records wash and drying, but the required ATP result is blank and the quality-release signature is absent.
state.request: Decide release readiness, delay-risk level, and the support function that should receive the case.

reference.reason: The ingredients, tooling, maintenance, and staffing gates are complete, but the source cleaning record lacks both the ATP result and quality-release signature. The supervisor’s paraphrase cannot substitute for those records, so release must be denied and routed to Quality at critical risk.

criteria.false: No — classify the changeover Amber or Red, do not release the line, and route the unresolved item to the responsible support function.
criteria.true: Yes — classify the changeover Green and release the line to production because every required readiness item has explicit evidence.

decision.instructions: Decide whether the line may be released to production now. Apply this rubric: Green means every scheduled material, required staffing level, signed cleaning record, correct tooling, passed quality prerequisite, and closed maintenance work order with recorded torque and technician signature has explicit evidence; release is Yes. Amber means only documentation or verification remains and release is No, routed to the responsible support function. Red means a physical resource, safety repair, cleaning, or quality result is missing and release is No. Is the line Green and releasable now?

criteria.false: No — do not release Line 4 because at least one required readiness condition is incomplete or an unresolved maintenance defect remains.
criteria.true: Yes — release Line 4 because every required readiness condition is complete and no unresolved maintenance defect remains.

input.state: At fictional Northstar Components, Line 4 is scheduled to change from blue valve caps to white caps at 14:00. Materials support staged all required white resin and labels. criteria: Level 0 — Ready, low delay risk: Every stated release condition has documented completion or approval; release the line at the scheduled time.

Level 1 — Conditional readiness, moderate delay risk: No confirmed failure exists, but at least one stated release condition lacks completion evidence; hold release and route to the responsible function.
Level 2 — Not ready, high delay risk: At least one stated release condition has failed, required resources are unavailable, or an active maintenance or quality hold exists; do not release.
decision.instructions: Apply the scheduler’s conditional release intent literally. Select the single level whose definition matches the documented status; lower levels mean lower delay risk.

state.context: At 06:45, the Line 4 changeover from 500 mL bottles to 750 mL bottles is scheduled to finish for a 07:00 production start. The production scheduler stated: release at 07:00 only if all materials are staged, tooling verification is complete, cleaning is accepted, required staff are present, and quality checks pass.

state.request: Using the ordered delay-risk rubric, determine the readiness level and whether Line 4 should be released at 07:00.

Therefore the conditional release criterion is satisfied and the line should be released at 07:00.

decision.instructions: Determine changeover readiness as of 06:52. Later timestamped updates supersede earlier reports about the same issue. Mandatory release gates are: enough material for the first lot, installed tooling, signed cleaning record, four operators, quality approval, and no current stop-work hold. Select the single matching level; its stated routing and release decision apply.

criteria.address_clarification: Route for address clarification only when the destination cannot be verified or conflicting location details prevent identifying the intended stop.
criteria.damage_review: Route to damage review only when a scan, driver observation, or package inspection indicates actual or suspected damage.
criteria.depot_hold: Route to depot hold only when the recipient requests collection from the depot or policy forbids another delivery attempt.
criteria.redelivery: Route for redelivery when the address is verified, the package is sound, access failed for a temporary reason, and the recipient requests another attempt.

decision.instructions: Choose exactly one route. Interpret the recipient’s wording by meaning rather than requiring an exact policy phrase.

state.context: A route dispatcher is reviewing an exception with the delivery driver, depot operations lead, and customer service agent. Apply the route policy in the options and treat synonymous wording as equivalent evidence.
evidence: Dispatch record: stop 42, 18 Vale Street, due today; vehicle is a 2.3 m van.
Stop instruction: use the 2.4 m loading bay, not the resident garage.
Scans: arrived 14:06; access exception 14:12; no damage scan.
Driver note: bay taped off for construction; security pointed to a 2.1 m garage, which the van could not enter.
Recipient answered the driver’s call and said, “Try me again after 10 tomorrow”; package remained sealed and dry.
state.request: Which single exception route is eligible now?

reference.reason: The address is verified, the sealed and dry package has no damage evidence, and the obstruction is temporary. “Try me again after 10 tomorrow” paraphrases a request for another delivery attempt, so redelivery is eligible.

criteria.address_clarification: Choose only when no damage-review condition applies and the recorded delivery address is conflicting or unverified.
criteria.customer_contact: Choose only when no earlier condition applies and access details required to perform the stop are missing.
criteria.damage_review: Choose first only when recorded evidence shows a crush over 2.0 cm, a leak, an opening, or rattling.
criteria.depot_hold: Choose only when neither prior condition applies and there have been at least two failed attempts or a recorded vehicle restriction prevents service.
criteria.redelivery: Choose only when no earlier condition applies, the address and access details are usable, and another delivery attempt is feasible.

decision.instructions: Select the required exception route by applying the stated first-match routing order. Treat threshold language literally and rely only on the identified recorded evidence.

state.speaker: Route dispatcher
state.text: Stop 42 has the correct verified address, lift-gate access instructions, and no vehicle restriction. It is attempt one; the recipient was absent at 14:10 but confirms availability tomorrow.

state.speaker: Delivery driver
state.text: I scanned “recipient unavailable.” My photo and note show one corner crushed exactly 2.0 cm; the seal is intact, with no leak, opening, or rattling.

state.speaker: Depot operations lead
state.text: Use recorded evidence only. In order: damage review for a crush over 2.0 cm, leak, opening, or rattle; address clarification for an address conflict; depot hold after two failed attempts or a vehicle restriction; customer contact for missing access details; otherwise redelivery.

state.speaker: Customer service agent
state.text: The recipient later said by phone that the box was “probably ruined,” but supplied no photo or inspection evidence.

reference.reason: Redelivery is required. The documented crush is exactly 2.0 cm, not over 2.0 cm, and no other qualifying damage is recorded. The address and access details are valid, there is no vehicle restriction, and this was only the first failed attempt. The recipient’s unsupported damage claim does not count as evidence.

criteria.false: No means redelivery is prohibited or unsupported and another route, here depot hold, is required.
criteria.true: Yes means the record and stated policy make redelivery the correct exception route.

decision.instructions: Decide whether this exception should be routed for redelivery. Apply the stop instruction exactly: recipient unavailability requires depot hold and explicitly prohibits redelivery unless an alternate-delivery request exists. Answer yes or no.

criteria.true: Route the incident to address clarification because the condition in the dispatcher’s instruction was confirmed.

state.context: Package ZX-418 is on Route 12 for 8 Harbor Lane, Unit 4B. Delivery driver: Concierge said the recipient moved to Unit 7C last month.

Scan events show arrival and unsuccessful delivery, with no completion scan.

state.request: Under depot policy, should this exception be routed to address clarification rather than redelivery?

criteria: 0 — Damage review: Current evidence shows or still reasonably indicates package damage, leakage, broken seals, or uncertain contents; movement and completion are blocked pending inspection.

1 — Address clarification: The package is serviceable, but the recorded destination conflicts with site evidence or an unverified correction; route for verified address resolution, and completion eligibility is no.

2 — Redelivery or depot hold: The address is verified and the package is serviceable, but a temporary recipient-availability, timing, or vehicle/access constraint prevents completion; schedule redelivery or hold for collection.
3 — Completion eligible: The destination is verified, the package is serviceable, recipient and handoff requirements can be satisfied, and no vehicle, access, or timing exception remains.
decision.instructions: Assign the incident to one ordered resolution-readiness level. Use the latest timestamped update when it supersedes an earlier observation. An unverified address correction cannot be used for delivery. Completion eligibility requires a verified destination, compliance with handoff instructions, and no unresolved package or access exception.
